request.description:
REAL finding (not a scanner false positive), found while auditing the CISO package for the secrets-resolver increment. It is out of scope for that task, so it is recorded here.

## Evidence (api/codx/junior/security/github_oauth.py)
- L61 `logger.info("get_access_token %s", data)` — `data` contains `client_secret` and `code_verifier`, so the OAuth client secret is written to the container log on every login.
- L62-63 `query_string = "&".join(...)` then `requests.post(f"{token_url}?{query_string}")` — `client_secret` is placed in the URL QUERY STRING (not the body). It therefore also lands in: proxy/access logs, `err.request.url` which L67-70 logs via `logger.exception`, any tracing/APM capture, and the browser/HTTP history.
- Note: the CISO audit flagged this file at L50 (`secret.hardcoded-credential`) which is a FALSE positive (a URL literal). The real defect at L61-L63 was not flagged.

## What to do
1. Send the token exchange as a POST *body* (`requests.post(token_url, data=data, headers={"Accept": "application/json"})`), never in the query string.
2. Delete the `logger.info(... data ...)` line; if a log is needed, log only the grant type and a truncated `code` digest (see `redact_token` in `codx/junior/security/user_management.py`).
3. Never log `err.request.url` for this request; log the status code and a request id instead.
4. Rotate the GitHub OAuth client secret for every deployment that has already run this code — treat it as disclosed in logs.

## Acceptance criteria
- No `client_secret` value can appear in any log record from this module (add a test that captures `caplog` during `get_access_token` and asserts the secret is absent).
- The token exchange request carries no credentials in the request line.
- `security_audit` on `api/codx/junior/security/github_oauth.py` reports 0 findings above `low`.

"""Tests for the secrets resolver (``codx.junior.security.ciso.vault``).

The property under test is narrow and absolute: a resolved value must never
appear in the model-visible tool arguments, in a redacted result, in an audit
row, in ``repr()``/``str()`` or in the tool cache key. The fixtures are
obviously fake on purpose -- a test file must never need a real secret.
"""

import base64
import json
import urllib.parse

import pytest

from codx.junior.security.ciso import vault as secret_vault
from codx.junior.security.ciso.models import CisoPolicy, SecretPolicy

FAKE = "unit-test-value-1234"  # deliberately not secret-shaped
VAR = "UNIT_TEST_TOKEN"


def _policy(**overrides) -> CisoPolicy:
    """Return a policy whose secrets block is *overrides*."""
    return CisoPolicy(secrets=SecretPolicy(**overrides))


def test_handles_are_parsed():
    handles = list(secret_vault.iter_handles(
        {"env": {"A": "{{env:A}}"}, "command": "echo {{secret:B}}"}
    ))
    assert [(handle.name, handle.source) for _, _, handle in handles] == [("A", "env"), ("B", "secret")]


def test_env_handle_lands_in_env_only(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv(VAR, FAKE)
    params = {"command": "aws s3 ls", "env": {"AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY": f"{{{{env:{VAR}}}}}"}}
    result = secret_vault.resolve_for_tool(params, "execute_command", step_id="s1", policy=_policy())
    assert result.error is None
    assert result.params["env"]["AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY"] == FAKE
    assert result.params["command"] == "aws s3 ls"
    assert list(result.redactions) == [VAR]


def test_handle_inside_command_is_denied(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv(VAR, FAKE)
    params = {"command": f"curl https://example.test/{{{{env:{VAR}}}}}"}
    result = secret_vault.resolve_for_tool(params, "execute_command", policy=_policy())
    assert result.error is not None
    assert "denied_sink" in result.error
    assert FAKE not in result.error
    assert result.params["command"] == params["command"]


def test_handle_mixed_with_text_is_denied(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv(VAR, FAKE)
    params = {"env": {"A": f"prefix-{{{{env:{VAR}}}}}"}}
    result = secret_vault.resolve_for_tool(params, "execute_command", policy=_policy())
    assert "denied_sink" in (result.error or "")


def test_denied_tool_never_receives_a_secret(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv(VAR, FAKE)
    params = {"text": f"{{{{env:{VAR}}}}}"}
    result = secret_vault.resolve_for_tool(params, "fetch_webpage", policy=_policy())
    assert "denied_sink" in (result.error or "")
    params = {"env": {"A": f"{{{{env:{VAR}}}}}"}}
    result = secret_vault.resolve_for_tool(params, "fetch_webpage", policy=_policy())
    assert "denied_tool" in (result.error or "")


def test_vault_source_requires_a_grant(tmp_path):
    vault = secret_vault.SecretVault(str(tmp_path), _policy())
    resolved = vault.resolve("ANY_SECRET", tool="execute_command", step_id="s", sink="env",
                             source="secret")
    assert isinstance(resolved, secret_vault.SecretError)
    assert resolved.code in {"denied_tool", "vault_unavailable"}


def test_resolved_value_never_renders(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv(VAR, FAKE)
    vault = secret_vault.SecretVault("/tmp", _policy())
    resolved = vault.resolve(VAR, tool="execute_command", step_id="s", sink="env", source="env")
    assert resolved.value == FAKE
    assert FAKE not in repr(resolved)
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        str(resolved)


def test_redaction_covers_base64_and_urlencoding():
    redactions = secret_vault.RedactionSet([("T", FAKE)])
    encoded = base64.b64encode(FAKE.encode()).decode()
    quoted = urllib.parse.quote(FAKE, safe="")
    masked = redactions.mask(" ".join([FAKE, encoded, quoted]))
    assert FAKE not in masked
    assert masked.count("***[secret:T]***") == 3


def test_redact_result_scrubs_a_tool_response():
    class Response:
        user_response = f"token={FAKE}"
        llm_response = f"used {FAKE}"
        logs = [f"export T={FAKE}"]

    redacted = secret_vault.redact_result(Response(), secret_vault.RedactionSet([("T", FAKE)]))
    assert FAKE not in redacted.user_response + redacted.llm_response + "".join(redacted.logs)


def test_audit_row_holds_the_name_not_the_value(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    monkeypatch.setenv(VAR, FAKE)
    vault = secret_vault.SecretVault(str(tmp_path), _policy())
    vault.resolve(VAR, tool="execute_command", step_id="s1", sink="env", source="env")
    payload = open(vault.audit_path, "r", encoding="utf-8").read()
    row = json.loads(payload.strip().splitlines()[-1])
    assert row["secret"] == VAR
    assert row["event"] == "resolve"
    assert FAKE not in payload


def test_list_never_enumerates_the_environment(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    monkeypatch.setenv("SOME_UNDECLARED_VARIABLE", FAKE)
    vault = secret_vault.SecretVault(str(tmp_path), _policy())
    assert vault.list() == []

"""Data models for the CISO security subsystem.

The CISO subsystem answers one question everywhere in the platform: *may this
artifact, command or answer cross the trust boundary?*

Three design rules make the answer trustworthy:

* **Deterministic.** Detectors use regular expressions, entropy and structural
  heuristics. No security decision is delegated to an LLM, so a verdict is
  reproducible, cheap and auditable (it can be replayed against a stored diff).
* **Two stages.** *Detectors* only produce :class:`SecurityFinding` signals.
  The *policy engine* (:mod:`codx.junior.security.ciso.policy`) turns the
  signals into a single :class:`SecurityVerdict`. Severity therefore never
  implies an action by itself: the same HIGH finding may block a git commit and
  only warn inside a document.
* **Dependency-free.** These models are plain dataclasses on purpose: the
  package must import on *any* interpreter, because the very same code runs
  inside the API, in a git hook (often from a worktree with no virtualenv), in
  a container image and in CI. A security gate that needs the application
  dependency tree is a gate that stops running exactly when it is needed: it
  dies with an ``ImportError`` at commit time instead of scanning.

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior
"""

import copy as _copy
from dataclasses import dataclass, fields as _dataclass_fields
from enum import Enum
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, get_args, get_origin

_NONE_TYPE = type(None)


@dataclass
class CisoModel:
    """Base class of the CISO models: plain dataclasses, no third-party import.

    It exposes the three attributes the rest of the package (and the tools)
    expect from a model, so replacing the previous pydantic base changed no
    call site:

    * ``model_dump(mode="json")`` -> JSON-safe ``dict`` (enums become values),
    * ``to_dict()`` / ``dict()`` -> the same, for older callers,
    * ``model_copy(update={...})`` -> a copy with fields overridden.

    Values are coerced to their declared enum or nested model on construction,
    which keeps a verdict loaded from ``.codx`` JSON working when its enums come
    back as plain strings.
    """

    def model_dump(self, mode: str = "python", **_: Any) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Return the model as a ``dict`` (``mode="json"`` stringifies enums)."""
        return _plain(self, json_mode=(mode == "json"))

    def dict(self, **kwargs: Any) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Alias of :meth:`model_dump`, kept for pydantic-v1 style callers."""
        return self.model_dump(**kwargs)

    def model_copy(
        self, update: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None, deep: bool = False
    ) -> "CisoModel":
        """Return a copy of this model, optionally with *update* applied."""
        clone = _copy.deepcopy(self) if deep else _copy.copy(self)
        for key, value in (update or {}).items():
            setattr(clone, key, value)
        return clone

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        """Coerce every field to its declared enum/nested-model type."""
        for model_field in _dataclass_fields(self):
            value = getattr(self, model_field.name)
            setattr(self, model_field.name, _coerce(value, model_field.type))


def _coerce_enum(value: Any, enum_type: type) -> Any:
    """Return *value* as a member of *enum_type* when it can be resolved."""
    if value is None or isinstance(value, enum_type):
        return value
    if isinstance(value, str):
        for member in enum_type:
            if value == member.value or value.lower() == member.name.lower():
                return member
    return value


def _coerce(value: Any, hint: Any) -> Any:
    """Coerce *value* to *hint* (enum, nested model or list of them)."""
    if value is None or hint is Any:
        return value
    if hint is int or hint is float:
        if isinstance(value, str) and value.strip().lstrip("-").isdigit():
            return hint(value)
        return value
    origin = get_origin(hint)
    if origin is not None:
        args = get_args(hint)
        if origin is list or origin is List:
            item_hint = args[0] if args else Any
            if isinstance(value, (list, tuple)):
                return [_coerce(item, item_hint) for item in value]
            return value
        # Optional[X] / Union[...]: coerce with the first matching member.
        for arg in args:
            if arg is _NONE_TYPE or arg is type(None):
                continue
            coerced = _coerce(value, arg)
            if coerced is not value:
                return coerced
        return value
    if isinstance(hint, type):
        if issubclass(hint, Enum):
            return _coerce_enum(value, hint)
        if issubclass(hint, CisoModel) and isinstance(value, dict):
            return hint(**value)
    return value


def _plain(value: Any, json_mode: bool) -> Any:
    """Return *value* with models expanded to dicts (and enums to values)."""
    if isinstance(value, Enum):
        return value.value if json_mode else value
    if isinstance(value, CisoModel):
        return {
            model_field.name: _plain(getattr(value, model_field.name), json_mode)
            for model_field in _dataclass_fields(value)
        }
    if isinstance(value, (list, tuple)):
        return [_plain(item, json_mode) for item in value]
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return {key: _plain(item, json_mode) for key, item in value.items()}
    return value

    """Severity of a single CISO finding."""

    INFO = "info"

    MEDIUM = "medium"
    HIGH = "high"

SEVERITY_RANK: Dict[SecuritySeverity, int] = {
    SecuritySeverity.INFO: 0,
    SecuritySeverity.LOW: 1,
    SecuritySeverity.MEDIUM: 2,
    SecuritySeverity.HIGH: 3,
    SecuritySeverity.CRITICAL: 4,

    """
    Coerce *value* to a :class:`SecuritySeverity`.

    Args:
        value: A ``SecuritySeverity``, its string name/value, or ``None``.

    Returns:
        The severity, or ``None`` when the value is empty or unknown.

    if isinstance(value, SecuritySeverity):
        return value
    raw = str(value or "").strip().lower()
    if not raw:
        return None
    for severity in SecuritySeverity:
        if raw in (severity.value, severity.name.lower()):
            return severity
    return None

    severity: Optional[SecuritySeverity],
    minimum: Optional[SecuritySeverity],
) -> bool:
    """Return True when *severity* is at least *minimum*."""

        return True
    return severity_rank(severity) >= severity_rank(minimum)

        """Return a JSON serialisable representation."""

    def findings_by_severity(self) -> Dict[str, int]:
        """Count the findings per severity (useful for reports)."""
        counts: Dict[str, int] = {}
        for finding in self.findings:
            key = finding.severity.value
            counts[key] = counts.get(key, 0) + 1
        return counts

    def findings_at_least(
        self, minimum: Optional[SecuritySeverity]
    ) -> List[SecurityFinding]:
        """
        Return the findings whose severity is at least *minimum*.

        Args:
            minimum: Severity floor; ``None`` keeps every finding.

        Returns:
            List[SecurityFinding]: Findings sorted by descending severity.
        """
        kept = [f for f in self.findings if meets_minimum(f.severity, minimum)]
        return sorted(kept, key=lambda f: severity_rank(f.severity), reverse=True)

    def filtered(self, minimum: Optional[SecuritySeverity]) -> "SecurityVerdict":
        """
        Return a copy of this verdict keeping only findings >= *minimum*.

        The risk score, the action and the domain are preserved (they were
        computed from the whole payload); only the finding list and the highest
        severity are recomputed, so a filtered verdict can be rendered safely.
        """
        if minimum is None:
            return self
        kept = self.findings_at_least(minimum)
        highest = max(
            (finding.severity for finding in kept),
            key=severity_rank,
            default=None,
        )
        return self.model_copy(
            update={"findings": kept, "highest_severity": highest}
        )

    """Severities that always block, in every domain."""
    return [SecuritySeverity.CRITICAL]


def _default_block_categories() -> List[SecurityCategory]:
    """Categories blocked once they reach ``block_above``."""
    return [
        SecurityCategory.SECRET,
        SecurityCategory.MALICIOUS,
        SecurityCategory.DATA_EXFILTRATION,

def _default_strict_domains() -> List[SecurityDomain]:
    """Domains where a finding at ``block_above`` blocks instead of asking."""
    # Every domain that PERSISTS or EXECUTES an artifact. A file write belongs
    # here with the git ones: writing the file is what puts the secret on disk,
    # so redacting it and continuing would leave the repository one `git add`
    # away from the incident.
    return [
        SecurityDomain.FILE_WRITE,
        SecurityDomain.GIT_COMMIT,
        SecurityDomain.PULL_REQUEST,
        SecurityDomain.COMMAND,
        SecurityDomain.CONTAINER,
        SecurityDomain.DEPLOY,
    ]


def _default_ignore_paths() -> List[str]:
    """Path fragments skipped by the file scanners (vendored/generated)."""
    return [
        "node_modules/", "dist/", "build/", ".venv/", "venv/",
        "__pycache__/", ".mypy_cache/", ".pytest_cache/", "package-lock.json",
        "poetry.lock", "yarn.lock",
    ]


def _default_denied_tools() -> List[str]:
    """Tools that may never receive a secret, whatever the grant says.

    Two families: tools whose OUTPUT is model-visible text (a value passed in is
    echoed back) and tools that PERSIST their arguments (a file, a task body, a
    knowledge entry), which would write the credential into the repository. A
    trailing ``*`` is a prefix match.

    return [
        "fetch_webpage*", "web_search*", "web_fetch*",
        "security_*",
        "project_write_file*", "apply_file_changes*", "code_writer*",
        "create_task*", "project_manager*",
        "profile_*", "knowledge_*",
    ]

"""CISO policy engine: turn findings into one deterministic decision.

Detectors produce signals; this module decides what happens with them. Keeping
the decision here means every integration point (file write, commit, command,
model output, knowledge ingestion) applies the *same* rule set, and a policy
change is a single edit.

Decision ladder
    ALLOW             nothing reached ``warn_above``
    WARN              findings above ``warn_above`` only, the operation proceeds
    REQUIRE_APPROVAL  findings above ``approval_above``: a human must confirm
    BLOCK             a ``block_severities`` finding, a blocked category above
                      ``block_above``, or any HIGH inside a ``strict_domain``
    REDACT            secrets were found and ``redact_secrets`` is on: the
                      payload may proceed only after the redacted text is used

The engine is *fail-safe on the payload, fail-open on the platform*: a detector
crash never breaks a chat (the operation proceeds and the error is logged),
unless ``policy.fail_closed`` is set.

import os
from typing import Any, Dict, Iterable, List, Optional

    SecretPolicy,
    SecurityAction,
    SecurityCategory,
    SecurityDomain,
    SecurityFinding,
    SecuritySeverity,
    SecurityVerdict,

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Numeric rank of each severity, used for threshold comparisons.
SEVERITY_RANK: Dict[SecuritySeverity, int] = {
    SecuritySeverity.INFO: 0,
    SecuritySeverity.LOW: 1,
    SecuritySeverity.MEDIUM: 2,
    SecuritySeverity.HIGH: 3,
    SecuritySeverity.CRITICAL: 4,
}

# Weight of each severity in the risk score of a verdict.
SEVERITY_WEIGHTS: Dict[SecuritySeverity, float] = {
    SecuritySeverity.INFO: 0.0,
    SecuritySeverity.LOW: 1.0,
    SecuritySeverity.MEDIUM: 3.0,
    SecuritySeverity.HIGH: 7.0,
    SecuritySeverity.CRITICAL: 25.0,
}

# Environment variable to disable the whole subsystem in an emergency.
POLICY_DISABLE_ENV = "CODX_JUNIOR_CISO_DISABLED"

# Settings key (project or global settings JSON) holding the policy overrides.
POLICY_SETTINGS_KEY = "ciso_policy"


def severity_rank(severity: Optional[SecuritySeverity]) -> int:
    """Return the numeric rank of *severity* (``-1`` when unknown)."""
    if severity is None:
        return -1
    return SEVERITY_RANK.get(severity, -1)


def highest_severity(findings: Iterable[SecurityFinding]) -> Optional[SecuritySeverity]:
    """Return the highest severity among *findings*, or ``None``."""
    best: Optional[SecuritySeverity] = None
    for finding in findings:
        if best is None or severity_rank(finding.severity) > severity_rank(best):
            best = finding.severity
    return best


def risk_score(findings: Iterable[SecurityFinding]) -> float:
    """Return the aggregated risk score of *findings*."""
    return round(sum(SEVERITY_WEIGHTS.get(f.severity, 0.0) for f in findings), 2)


def _coerce_enum_values(values: Any, enum_cls) -> List[Any]:
    """Coerce a list of strings/enums into *enum_cls*, ignoring invalid items."""
    coerced = []
    for value in values or []:
        try:
            coerced.append(value if isinstance(value, enum_cls) else enum_cls(value))
        except (ValueError, TypeError):
            logger.warning("CISO policy: ignoring unknown %s value %r", enum_cls.__name__, value)
    return coerced


def policy_from_dict(data: Optional[Dict[str, Any]]) -> CisoPolicy:
    """Build a :class:`CisoPolicy` from a partial settings dictionary.

    Unknown keys are ignored so a settings file written for a newer version
    never breaks the platform.

    Args:
        data: Partial policy (e.g. ``{"block_above": "medium"}``).

    Returns:
        CisoPolicy: Policy with the defaults merged with *data*.
    """
    policy = CisoPolicy()
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        return policy

    simple_fields = {
        "enabled", "redact_secrets", "fail_closed", "entropy_threshold",
        "min_secret_length", "max_scan_bytes", "max_excerpt_chars",
    }
    for field in simple_fields:
        if field in data and data[field] is not None:
            setattr(policy, field, data[field])

    for field in ("ignore_paths", "ignore_rules", "allow_secret_files"):
        if isinstance(data.get(field), list):
            setattr(policy, field, [str(item) for item in data[field]])

    for field, enum_cls in (
        ("block_severities", SecuritySeverity),
        ("block_categories", SecurityCategory),
        ("strict_domains", SecurityDomain),
        ("enabled_domains", SecurityDomain),
    ):
        if isinstance(data.get(field), list):
            setattr(policy, field, _coerce_enum_values(data[field], enum_cls))

    for field, enum_cls in (
        ("block_above", SecuritySeverity),
        ("approval_above", SecuritySeverity),
        ("warn_above", SecuritySeverity),
    ):
        if data.get(field):
            coerced = _coerce_enum_values([data[field]], enum_cls)
            if coerced:
                setattr(policy, field, coerced[0])

    # Nested block: unknown keys are dropped instead of raising, so a settings
    # file written for a newer version still loads.
    secrets_data = data.get("secrets")
    if isinstance(secrets_data, dict):
        try:
            policy.secrets = SecretPolicy(
                **{
                    key: value
                    for key, value in secrets_data.items()
                    if key in SecretPolicy.__dataclass_fields__

        except Exception as ex:
            logger.warning("CISO policy: ignoring invalid 'secrets' block: %s", ex)

    return policy

    settings, defaults. Any error degrades to the default policy.

    Args:

            ``get_project_config``/``settings``).

    Returns:
        CisoPolicy: Effective policy.
    """
    if (os.environ.get(POLICY_DISABLE_ENV) or "").strip().lower() in {"1", "true", "yes", "on"}:
        policy = CisoPolicy()
        policy.enabled = False
        return policy

    data: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None
    if settings is not None:
        try:
            project_config = getattr(settings, "settings", None)
            if isinstance(project_config, dict):
                candidate = project_config.get(POLICY_SETTINGS_KEY)
                if isinstance(candidate, dict):
                    data = candidate
        except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
            logger.warning("CISO policy: could not read project settings: %s", ex)

    return policy_from_dict(data)


def evaluate(
    findings: List[SecurityFinding],
    domain: SecurityDomain = SecurityDomain.FILE_WRITE,
    policy: Optional[CisoPolicy] = None,
    redacted_text: Optional[str] = None,
    rules_evaluated: int = 0,
    truncated: bool = False,
) -> SecurityVerdict:
    """Apply the policy to *findings* and return the verdict.

    Args:
        findings: Signals produced by the detectors.
        domain: Integration point the check ran in.
        policy: Effective policy (defaults when omitted).
        redacted_text: Sanitised payload when secrets were neutralised.
        rules_evaluated: Number of rules that ran (reported for transparency).
        truncated: True when the scanned payload was cut to the size cap.

    Returns:
        SecurityVerdict: The deterministic decision.
    """
    policy = policy or CisoPolicy()
    severity = highest_severity(findings)
    score = risk_score(findings)

    verdict = SecurityVerdict(
        domain=domain,
        findings=findings,
        risk_score=score,
        highest_severity=severity,
        rules_evaluated=rules_evaluated,
        truncated=truncated,
        redacted_text=redacted_text,
    )

    if not findings:
        verdict.action = SecurityAction.ALLOW
        verdict.allowed = True
        verdict.summary = "No security findings."
        return verdict

    ranking = severity_rank(severity)
    strict = domain in policy.strict_domains
    has_secret = any(f.category == SecurityCategory.SECRET for f in findings)
    # A finding that blocks in ANY domain: the severity the policy declares as
    # blocking, for a category that is not a secret (secrets have their own
    # treatment, because they can be neutralised instead of refused).
    hard_non_secret = any(
        f.severity in policy.block_severities
        and f.category != SecurityCategory.SECRET
        for f in findings
    )
    # 1. Strict domains (commit, file write, command, container, deploy) block
    #    every finding at or above `block_above`: nothing is persisted or
    #    executed there, so there is no "approve and continue" shortcut.
    if strict and ranking >= severity_rank(policy.block_above):
        verdict.action = SecurityAction.BLOCK
        verdict.blocked = True
        verdict.allowed = False

    # 2. A neutralised secret may proceed with the redacted payload. Blocking a
    #    model answer, a document or a log line because it quoted a key that has
    #    already been replaced costs the user the content and protects nothing.
    elif has_secret and policy.redact_secrets and redacted_text is not None:
        if hard_non_secret:
            verdict.action = SecurityAction.BLOCK
            verdict.blocked = True
            verdict.allowed = False
        else:
            verdict.action = SecurityAction.REDACT
            verdict.allowed = True
            verdict.requires_approval = True

    # 3. Destructive or exfiltrating content, and a CRITICAL secret we could not
    #    neutralise (no redacted payload), block everywhere.
    elif hard_non_secret or (
        has_secret and ranking >= severity_rank(SecuritySeverity.CRITICAL)
    ):
        verdict.action = SecurityAction.BLOCK
        verdict.blocked = True
        verdict.allowed = False

    # 4. Ask a human.
    elif ranking >= severity_rank(policy.approval_above):
        verdict.action = SecurityAction.REQUIRE_APPROVAL
        verdict.allowed = True
        verdict.requires_approval = True

    # 5. Warn.
    elif ranking >= severity_rank(policy.warn_above):
        verdict.action = SecurityAction.WARN
        verdict.allowed = True

    else:
        verdict.action = SecurityAction.ALLOW
        verdict.allowed = True

    verdict.summary = summarize(verdict)
    return verdict


def summarize(verdict: SecurityVerdict) -> str:
    """Return a one line, human readable description of *verdict*.

    Args:
        verdict: Verdict to describe.

    Returns:
        str: Summary line, e.g. ``block | critical | 2 finding(s) | secret``.
    """
    if not verdict.findings:
        return "clean"
    categories = sorted({f.category.value for f in verdict.findings})
    severity = verdict.highest_severity.value if verdict.highest_severity else "unknown"
    return (
        f"{verdict.action.value} | {severity} | "
        f"{len(verdict.findings)} finding(s) | {', '.join(categories)}"
    )

            header keeps the totals of the unfiltered scan plus the number of
            findings displayed, so a filtered report can never look cleaner
            than the scan that produced it.

    Returns:
        str: Markdown report with a redacted evidence column only.
    """
    total_findings = len(verdict.findings)
    if min_severity is not None:
        verdict = verdict.filtered(min_severity)
    icon = {
        SecurityAction.ALLOW: "✅",
        SecurityAction.WARN: "⚠️",
        SecurityAction.REDACT: "🟡",
        SecurityAction.REQUIRE_APPROVAL: "🟠",
        SecurityAction.BLOCK: "⛔",
    }.get(verdict.action, "•")

    lines = [
        f"# {title}",
        "",
        f"- Domain: `{verdict.domain.value}`",
        f"- Decision: {icon} **{verdict.action.value}**",
        f"- Highest severity: **{(verdict.highest_severity or SecuritySeverity.INFO).value}**",
        f"- Risk score: {verdict.risk_score}",
        f"- Findings: {len(verdict.findings)} ({verdict.findings_by_severity() or 'none'})",
        f"- Rules evaluated: {verdict.rules_evaluated}",
    ]
    if min_severity is not None:
        lines.insert(
            5,
            f"- Severity floor: **{min_severity.value}** "
            f"({len(verdict.findings)} of {total_findings} finding(s) shown)",
        )
    if verdict.truncated:
        lines.append("- ⚠️ The payload was truncated: only the beginning was scanned")
    lines.append("")

    if not verdict.findings:
        lines += ["No findings: the payload matches no CISO rule.", ""]
        return "\n".join(lines)

    lines += [
        "| Severity | Rule | Location | Evidence (redacted) | Remediation |",
        "| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |",
    ]
    for finding in verdict.findings[:max_findings]:
        location = finding.path or "-"
        if finding.line:
            location = f"{location}:{finding.line}"
        evidence = (finding.evidence or finding.excerpt or "").replace("|", "\\|")
        remediation = (finding.remediation or "").replace("|", "\\|")
        lines.append(
            f"| {finding.severity.value} | `{finding.rule_id}` | `{location}` | "
            f"{evidence} | {remediation} |"
        )
    if len(verdict.findings) > max_findings:
        lines.append(f"\n_… {len(verdict.findings) - max_findings} more finding(s) omitted._")

    lines += [
        "",
        "> Evidence is redacted: a detected secret is never reproduced in a report.",
        "",
    ]
    return "\n".join(lines)

    os.environ.get("CODX_JUNIOR_CISO_REDACT_CACHE_CHARS", str(64 * 1024 * 1024))

_REDACT_CACHE: "OrderedDict[bytes, Tuple[str, int, int]]" = OrderedDict()

    """Drop every cached redaction (tests / policy reloads)."""

    with _REDACT_CACHE_LOCK:
        _REDACT_CACHE.clear()
        _REDACT_CACHE_CHARS = 0

    """Return a cached ``(redacted, replacements)`` and mark it recently used."""

        if entry is None:
            return None
        _REDACT_CACHE.move_to_end(key)
        return entry[0], entry[1]


def _cache_store(key: bytes, cost: int, value: Tuple[str, int]) -> None:
    """Store one redaction under a bounded total-size budget."""
    global _REDACT_CACHE_CHARS
    if cost > _REDACT_CACHE_MAX_CHARS:
        return
    with _REDACT_CACHE_LOCK:
        previous = _REDACT_CACHE.pop(key, None)
        if previous is not None:
            _REDACT_CACHE_CHARS -= previous[2]
        _REDACT_CACHE[key] = (value[0], value[1], cost)
        _REDACT_CACHE_CHARS += cost
        while _REDACT_CACHE_CHARS > _REDACT_CACHE_MAX_CHARS and _REDACT_CACHE:
            _, evicted = _REDACT_CACHE.popitem(last=False)
            _REDACT_CACHE_CHARS -= evicted[2]
        if _REDACT_CACHE_CHARS < 0:  # defensive: never report a negative size
            _REDACT_CACHE_CHARS = 0


def shannon_entropy(value: str) -> float:
    """Return the Shannon entropy (bits per character) of *value*.

    Args:
        value: Text to measure.

    Returns:
        float: Entropy in bits/char; ``0.0`` for an empty string.

    Example:
        >>> round(shannon_entropy("aaaaaaaa"), 2)
        0.0
        >>> shannon_entropy("aB3$xY9!qW2&zR5%") > 3
        True
    """
    if not value:
        return 0.0
    counts = Counter(value)
    length = len(value)
    return -sum((count / length) * math.log2(count / length) for count in counts.values())

    """Return True when *path* is a file conventionally holding credentials.

    Args:

    Returns:
        bool: True for ``.env``, ``*.pem``, ``id_rsa``, ``.npmrc``, ...

    Example:
        >>> is_secret_file("config/.env.production")
        True
        >>> is_secret_file("src/app.py")
        False
    """
    if not path:
        return False
    normalised = path.replace("\\", "/")
    return any(pattern.search(normalised) for pattern in _SECRET_FILE_PATTERNS)


def looks_like_path(value: str) -> bool:
    """Return True when *value* is a file path rather than a credential.

    Filesystem paths are the largest single source of false positives for the
    entropy detector: ``codx/junior/security/ciso/gate.py`` or
    ``/home/user/projects/my-api`` are long, low-redundancy and full of
    separators. A credential is not usually shaped like a path, so a candidate
    that is one is rejected.

    Args:
        value: Candidate secret value.

    Returns:
        bool: True when the value looks like a path.
    """
    candidate = (value or "").strip()
    if not candidate:
        return False
    if candidate.startswith(("/", "~/", "./", "../")):
        return True
    if "://" in candidate:
        # A URL, not a filesystem path: the host has dots, but the value is a
        # credential the moment it embeds a user:password pair.
        return False
    if "/" not in candidate and "\\" not in candidate:
        return False
    normalised = candidate.replace("\\", "/")
    last_segment = normalised.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
    # ``docs/readme.md`` or ``codx/junior/app.py``: a dotted final segment.
    return "." in last_segment

# not one. Without this the gate blocks every file that documents the resolver
# syntax -- including the design doc and the tool schemas. See
# ``codx/junior/security/ciso/vault.py``.
_HANDLE_ONLY_PATTERN = re.compile(
    r"^\{\{\s*(?:secret|env)\s*:\s*[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.:@\-]{0,127}\s*\}\}$"
)


def is_secret_placeholder(value: str) -> bool:
    """Return True when *value* looks like a placeholder instead of a secret.

    Filters documentation examples, environment variable references and
    identifiers, which are the main source of false positives.

    Paths are also rejected: a long absolute project path
    (``/home/user/projects/my-project-api``) has enough entropy to look like a
    token, and every settings or config file written by the platform contains
    dozens of them.

    Args:
        value: Candidate secret value.

    Returns:
        bool: True when the value must not be reported.
    """
    candidate = (value or "").strip()
    if not candidate:
        return True
    # Already redacted by this module: ``mask()`` renders the value as
    # ``eyJh[REDACTED](24 chars)``. Reporting it again would leave a file that
    # was just cleaned still blocked, so the gate could never converge and the
    # only way out would be a permanent path allowlist.
    if REDACTED_MARKER in candidate:
        return True
    if _HANDLE_ONLY_PATTERN.match(candidate):
        # A handle names a secret; a later tool call resolves it.
        return True
    if len(candidate) < 8:
        return True
    if looks_like_path(candidate):
        # Filesystem path, not a credential.
        return True
    return any(pattern.search(candidate) for pattern in _PLACEHOLDER_PATTERNS)


def _redact(value: str) -> str:
    """Render a detected secret in a shape that cannot be reused.

    A short prefix is kept so a human can tell *which* credential leaked in a
    report, while the remainder is unrecoverable.

    Args:
        value: Raw secret.

    Returns:
        str: Redacted representation.
    """
    text = (value or "").strip()
    if not text:
        return REDACTED_MARKER
    if len(text) <= 8:
        return REDACTED_MARKER
    return f"{text[:4]}{REDACTED_MARKER}({len(text)} chars)"


def _line_of(text: str, index: int) -> int:
    """Return the 1-based line number of *index* inside *text*."""
    return text.count("\n", 0, index) + 1


def _excerpt(text: str, start: int, end: int, max_chars: int) -> str:
    """Build a redacted, bounded excerpt around a match."""
    radius = max(20, max_chars // 2)
    left = max(0, start - radius)
    right = min(len(text), end + radius)
    excerpt = text[left:right].replace("\n", " ⏎ ")
    if len(excerpt) > max_chars:
        excerpt = excerpt[:max_chars] + "…"
    return excerpt


def redact_text(text: str, policy: Optional[CisoPolicy] = None) -> Tuple[str, int]:
    """Neutralise every detected secret inside *text*.

    the whole chat on every streamed chunk / tool event.

    Args:
        text: Payload to sanitise.
        policy: Optional policy (size and excerpt limits).

    Returns:
        tuple: ``(redacted_text, replacements)``. When nothing matched the
        original string is returned unchanged and replacements is ``0``.

    Example:
        >>> redact_text('password = "s3cr[REDACTED](17 chars)"')[0]
        'password = "s3cr…'
    """
    payload = text or ""
    if not payload:
        return "", 0

    # Base64 data URLs are binary bodies: scan only the text around them.
    # Cache only the default policy (a custom policy can change the result),
    # and skip the cache for tiny strings where the digest is not worth it.
    has_data_url = bool(_DATA_URL_PATTERN.search(payload))
    cacheable = (
        not has_data_url
        and policy is None
        and len(payload) >= _REDACT_CACHE_MIN_CHARS
    )
    key: Optional[bytes] = None
    if cacheable:
        # SHA-256: the cache returns a redaction result, so a collision must
        # stay cryptographically out of reach (BLAKE2 128-bit would also do,
        # but the extra bytes are cheaper than debating the margin).
        key = hashlib.sha256(
            payload.encode("utf-8", errors="replace")
        ).digest()
        cached = _cache_lookup(key)
        if cached is not None:
            return cached

    redacted, replacements = _redact_text_segments(payload, policy)
    if cacheable and key is not None:
        _cache_store(key, len(payload) + len(redacted), (redacted, replacements))
    return redacted, replacements


def _redact_text_segments(text: str, policy: Optional[CisoPolicy]) -> Tuple[str, int]:
    """Redact text while copying inline binary (base64 data URL) bodies verbatim."""
    if not _DATA_URL_PATTERN.search(text):
        return _redact_text_scan(text, policy)

    pieces: List[str] = []
    replacements = 0
    last = 0
    for match in _DATA_URL_PATTERN.finditer(text):
        chunk = text[last:match.start()]
        if chunk:
            redacted, found = _redact_text_scan(chunk, policy)
            pieces.append(redacted)
            replacements += found
        pieces.append(match.group(0))
        last = match.end()
    tail = text[last:]
    if tail:
        redacted, found = _redact_text_scan(tail, policy)
        pieces.append(redacted)
        replacements += found
    return "".join(pieces), replacements


def _redact_text_scan(text: str, policy: Optional[CisoPolicy]) -> Tuple[str, int]:
    """Run every detector over *text* (the original, non-cached implementation).

    Redaction rules are policy-independent (the policy decides what to BLOCK,
    not what to hide), so no ``CisoPolicy`` is materialised here: constructing
    one per string cost ~1 s on a real chat payload.
    """
    result = text or ""
    replacements = 0

    def _replace(match: re.Match) -> str:
        nonlocal replacements
        raw = match.group(0)
        if is_secret_placeholder(raw):
            return raw
        replacements += 1
        return _redact(raw)

    for _, _, _, pattern in _TOKEN_PATTERNS:
        result = pattern.sub(_replace, result)

    def _replace_assignment(match: re.Match) -> str:
        nonlocal replacements
        value = match.group("value")
        if is_secret_placeholder(value):
            return match.group(0)
        replacements += 1
        return match.group(0).replace(value, _redact(value))

    result = _ASSIGNMENT_PATTERN.sub(_replace_assignment, result)

    def _replace_url(match: re.Match) -> str:
        nonlocal replacements
        password = match.group("password")
        if is_secret_placeholder(password):
            return match.group(0)
        replacements += 1
        return match.group(0).replace(f":{password}@", f":{_redact(password)}@", 1)

    result = _URL_CREDENTIALS_PATTERN.sub(_replace_url, result)
    return result, replacements


def scan_text(
    text: str,
    path: Optional[str] = None,
    policy: Optional[CisoPolicy] = None,
) -> Tuple[List[SecurityFinding], str, bool]:
    """Detect secrets in *text*.

    Args:
        text: Payload to scan.
        path: File the payload belongs to (used for reporting and for the
            entropy relaxation inside documentation files).
        policy: Optional policy.

    Returns:
        tuple: ``(findings, redacted_text, truncated)``. The redacted text is
        safe to log and is what callers must store when they only need to keep
        a record of the payload.
    """
    policy = policy or CisoPolicy()
    payload = text or ""
    truncated = False
    if len(payload.encode("utf-8", errors="replace")) > policy.max_scan_bytes:
        payload = payload.encode("utf-8", errors="replace")[: policy.max_scan_bytes].decode(
            "utf-8", errors="replace"
        )
        truncated = True

    findings: List[SecurityFinding] = []

    def _add(
        rule_id: str,
        title: str,
        severity: SecuritySeverity,
        category: SecurityCategory,
        start: int,
        end: int,
        evidence: str,
        remediation: str,
    ) -> None:
        if policy.ignores_rule(rule_id):
            return
        findings.append(SecurityFinding(
            rule_id=rule_id,
            title=title,
            severity=severity,
            category=category,
            reason=f"Detected {title.lower()} in the payload",
            path=path,
            line=_line_of(payload, start),
            # The excerpt is copied into reports, logs and chat messages, so it
            # is redacted with the same rules as the evidence: a finding must
            # never reproduce the credential it reports.
            excerpt=_redact(_excerpt(payload, start, end, policy.max_excerpt_chars)),
            evidence=_redact(evidence),
            remediation=remediation,
            confidence=0.95,
        ))

    for rule_id, title, severity, pattern in _TOKEN_PATTERNS:
        for match in pattern.finditer(payload):
            # Same guard as `redact_text` and the rules below: a value the
            # redactor refuses to touch must not be reported either, otherwise
            # the gate reports a credential it cannot neutralise and the
            # cleanup never converges.
            if is_secret_placeholder(match.group(0)):
                continue
            _add(
                rule_id=rule_id,
                title=title,
                severity=severity,
                category=SecurityCategory.SECRET,
                start=match.start(),
                end=match.end(),
                evidence=match.group(0),
                remediation=(
                    "Remove the credential from the file, rotate it at the provider "
                    "and load it from the environment or the project secret store."
                ),
            )

    for match in _ASSIGNMENT_PATTERN.finditer(payload):
        value = match.group("value")
        if is_secret_placeholder(value):
            continue
        key = match.group("key")
        severity = SecuritySeverity.HIGH
        if (match.group("quote") == '"' or match.group("quote") == "'") and len(value) >= 16:
            severity = SecuritySeverity.CRITICAL
        _add(
            rule_id="secret.hardcoded-credential",
            title=f"Hardcoded credential in '{key}'",
            severity=severity,
            category=SecurityCategory.SECRET,
            start=match.start("value"),
            end=match.end("value"),
            evidence=value,
            remediation=(
                "Read the value from an environment variable or a secret manager "
                "and keep only a placeholder in the source file."
            ),
        )

    for match in _URL_CREDENTIALS_PATTERN.finditer(payload):
        password = match.group("password")
        if is_secret_placeholder(password):
            continue
        _add(
            rule_id="secret.url-embedded-credentials",
            title="Credentials embedded in a URL",
            severity=SecuritySeverity.CRITICAL,
            category=SecurityCategory.SECRET,
            start=match.start("password"),
            end=match.end("password"),
            evidence=password,
            remediation=(
                "Remove the user:password pair from the URL and pass the "
                "credential through a header or a secret reference."
            ),
        )

    if policy.entropy_threshold > 0:
        for match in _ENTROPY_CANDIDATE_PATTERN.finditer(payload):
            token = match.group(0)
            if len(token) < policy.min_secret_length:
                continue
            if is_secret_placeholder(token):
                continue
            # A long run of the same character class is usually an identifier,
            # a hash of a non-secret or an already redacted value.
            if REDACTED_MARKER in token:
                continue
            if shannon_entropy(token) < policy.entropy_threshold:
                continue
            _add(
                rule_id="secret.high-entropy-token",
                title="High entropy string (possible unknown token format)",
                severity=SecuritySeverity.MEDIUM,
                category=SecurityCategory.SECRET,
                start=match.start(),
                end=match.end(),
                evidence=token,
                remediation=(
                    "Confirm what this value is. If it is a credential, rotate it "
                    "and load it from the environment."
                ),
            )

    redacted, _ = redact_text(payload, policy)
    return findings, redacted, truncated

These are the tools the ``ciso`` profile (and any profile granted them) uses to
audit a project, review a change before it is committed or merged, validate a
payload before writing it, check a shell command and neutralise secrets in a
text that is about to be shared.

is the pull-request gate and ``security_check_command`` is the command gate.
Gates that run automatically inside a process live in
:mod:`codx.junior.security.ciso.gate`, not here: a tool is an explicit action,
a gate is an implicit guarantee.

def _settings_of(kwargs: Dict[str, Any]):

def _verdict_answer(verdict, title: str) -> str:

def _llm_summary(verdict, subject: str) -> str:
    """Build the compact machine friendly summary for the model."""
    lines = [
        f"# {subject}",
        f"- decision: {verdict.action.value}",
        f"- blocked: {verdict.blocked}",
        f"- requires_approval: {verdict.requires_approval}",
        f"- highest_severity: {(verdict.highest_severity.value if verdict.highest_severity else 'none')}",
        f"- risk_score: {verdict.risk_score}",
        f"- findings: {len(verdict.findings)}",
    ]
    for finding in verdict.findings[:10]:
        location = finding.path or "-"
        if finding.line:

        lines.append(
            f"- [{finding.severity.value}] {finding.rule_id} @ {location}: "
            f"{finding.remediation or finding.reason}"
        )
    if len(verdict.findings) > 10:
        lines.append(f"- … {len(verdict.findings) - 10} more finding(s)")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def _git_diff(settings: Any, base: str, scope: str, paths: Optional[List[str]]) -> str:
    """Return the unified diff requested by the caller.

    Args:
        settings: Project settings.
        base: Git reference to compare against.
        scope: ``all`` | ``staged`` | ``unstaged``.
        paths: Optional path filter.

    Returns:
        str: Unified diff (empty when there is nothing to review).
    """
    from .project_tools import _run_git

    args: List[str] = ["diff", "--no-ext-diff", "--no-textconv", "--no-color", "-U3"]
    if scope == "staged":
        args.append("--cached")
    elif scope == "all":
        args.append(base or "HEAD")

    if paths:
        args += ["--", *paths]

    ok, stdout, stderr = _run_git(settings, args)
    if not ok:
        raise ValueError(f"git diff failed: {(stderr or '').strip()}")
    return stdout or ""

def security_audit(
    path: Optional[str] = None,
    max_files: int = 200,
    include_dependency_files: bool = True,
    **kwargs
) -> ToolResponse:
    """Audit a project (or a sub path) for secrets, malicious code and injection.

    Scans the files of the project with every CISO detector and returns a
    Markdown report plus a machine friendly summary.

    Args:
        path: Optional project-relative folder or file to restrict the audit.
        max_files: Maximum number of files read (default 200).
        include_dependency_files: Also scan lock files / manifests
            (still skipped: vendored folders such as ``node_modules``).
        **kwargs: Runtime arguments; ``settings`` is injected automatically.

    if not settings:
        raise Exception("Invalid project settings")

    policy = resolve_policy(settings)

        absolute = path if os.path.isabs(path) else os.path.join(project_path, path)
        if os.path.isdir(absolute):
            from codx.junior.security.ciso.scanner import iter_project_files

            targets = iter_project_files(absolute, max_files=max_files, policy=policy)
        elif os.path.isfile(absolute):
            targets = [absolute]
        else:
            return ToolResponse(
                user_response=f"⚠️ Path not found: `{path}`",
                llm_response=f"security_audit: path not found: {path}",

        project_path,
        max_files=max_files,
        domain=SecurityDomain.FILE_READ,
        policy=policy,
        paths=targets,

    title = f"CISO audit — {getattr(settings, 'project_name', 'project')}"
    if path:
        title += f" — `{path}`"

        f"CISO audit: decision={verdict.action.value} blocked={verdict.blocked}",
    ]

            f"[{finding.severity.value.upper()}] {finding.rule_id} "
            f"{finding.path}:{finding.line or 0} — {finding.title}"

    returns a redacted version when it carries secrets.

        content: Exact payload to inspect.
        path: Target path (drives the reported location).

            ``model_output``, ``knowledge_ingestion``, ``profile``.

    """

    policy = resolve_policy(settings)

    try:

                          f"{', '.join(d.value for d in SecurityDomain)}",

    base: str = "HEAD",

    Args:
        base: Git reference to compare against (default ``HEAD``).

        >>> security_review_changes(scope="staged")  # doctest: +SKIP
    """
    settings = _settings_of(kwargs)
    if not settings:
        raise Exception("Invalid project settings")

    policy = resolve_policy(settings)
    domain = SecurityDomain.GIT_COMMIT if scope == "staged" else SecurityDomain.PULL_REQUEST

    try:
        patch = _git_diff(settings, base=base, scope=scope, paths=paths)
    except Exception as ex:
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response=f"⚠️ Could not read the change: {ex}",
            llm_response=f"security_review_changes: {ex}",
        )

    if not (patch or "").strip():
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response="✅ No pending changes to review.",
            llm_response="security_review_changes: empty diff, nothing to review.",
        )

    verdict = scan_diff(patch, domain=domain, policy=policy)
    return ToolResponse(
        user_response=_verdict_answer(verdict, f"CISO review — scope `{scope}` vs `{base}`"),
        llm_response=_llm_summary(verdict, "CISO change review"),
        logs=[f"CISO change review: {verdict.summary}"],
    )

def security_redact(text: str, **kwargs) -> ToolResponse:
    """Neutralise every detected secret inside *text*.

    Use it before sharing a log, a configuration file or a diff outside the
    project.

    Args:

    Returns:
        ToolResponse: user_response carries the redacted text; the summary
        reports how many values were replaced.

    Example:

    """

    return ToolResponse(
        user_response=redacted if replacements else "_No secret detected._\n\n" + (text or ""),
        llm_response=(
            f"{replacements} secret(s) redacted.\n\n```\n{redacted}\n```"
            if replacements
            else "No secret detected."

        logs=[f"CISO redact: {replacements} replacement(s)"],

def secrets_list(**kwargs) -> ToolResponse:
    """List the secrets the runtime can resolve — never their values.

    Use the returned names in a handle (``{{secret:NAME}}`` or ``{{env:NAME}}``)
    as the WHOLE value of the ``env`` map or of the ``stdin`` argument. A handle
    anywhere else (inside a command, a URL or a description) is refused.

    Args:
        **kwargs: Runtime injected settings.

    Returns:
        ToolResponse: The declared secrets with their availability.

    Example:
        >>> secrets_list()  # doctest: +SKIP
    """
    settings = _settings_of(kwargs)
    vault = ciso_vault.vault_for(settings)
    entries = vault.list()
    if not entries:
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response="No secret is declared for this project.",
            llm_response="secrets_list: no secret declared. Declare one with secrets_request.",
            logs=["CISO secrets: 0 declared"],
        )
    rows = [
        "| Name | Source | Status | Allowed tools | Description |",
        "| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |",
    ]
    for meta in entries:
        tools = ", ".join(meta.allow_tools) or "-"
        rows.append(
            f"| `{meta.name}` | {meta.source} | {meta.status} | {tools} | "
            f"{meta.description or '-'} |"
        )
    rows.append("")
    rows.append(
        "A handle must be the WHOLE value of `env.<NAME>` or `stdin`, e.g. "
        '`{"command": "docker login --password-stdin registry.local", '
        '"stdin": "{{secret:NAME}}"}`. A handle inside `command` is rejected.'
    )
    return ToolResponse(
        user_response="\n".join(rows),
        llm_response="\n".join(
            f"- {meta.name} [{meta.source}] {meta.status}" for meta in entries
        ),
        logs=[f"CISO secrets: {len(entries)} declared"],
    )


def secrets_request(name: str, reason: str = "", **kwargs) -> ToolResponse:
    """Declare that a secret is needed so the operator can provide it out of band.

    The value must never be typed into the chat: it would land in the message
    history, the index and the provider's logs. This creates a ``pending`` entry;
    ``secrets_list`` reports ``ready`` once the operator has stored it.

    Args:
        name: Secret name (identifier, e.g. ``REGISTRY_PASSWORD``).
        reason: Why the task needs it (shown to the operator).
        **kwargs: Runtime injected settings.

    Returns:
        ToolResponse: Instructions for the operator.

    Example:
        >>> secrets_request("REGISTRY_PASSWORD")  # doctest: +SKIP
    """
    settings = _settings_of(kwargs)
    vault = ciso_vault.vault_for(settings)
    meta = vault.request(name, chat_id=str(kwargs.get("chat_id") or ""), reason=reason)
    return ToolResponse(
        user_response=(
            f"### Secret `{meta.name}` requested\n\n"
            "Ask the operator to provide it **outside the chat**:\n\n"
            "```bash\n"
            "export CODX_JUNIOR_VAULT_KEY=...   # once, from: ... vault keygen\n"
            f"python -m codx.junior.security.ciso.vault add {meta.name} "
            "--tools execute_command\n"
            "```\n\n"
            "Never paste the value in a message. `secrets_list` reports `ready` "
            "once it is stored."
        ),
        llm_response=(
            f"secrets_request: '{meta.name}' is pending. The value is provided out of "
            "band by the operator — do not ask the user to type it in the chat, and "
            "never try to read it."
        ),
        logs=[f"CISO secrets: request '{meta.name}'"],
    )


def security_policy(action: str = "show", changes: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None, **kwargs) -> ToolResponse:
    """Show or adjust the CISO policy of the project.

    The policy is stored in the project settings under ``ciso_policy``. Only the
    fields listed in the report can be changed, and every change is validated
    against the policy model before it is applied.

    Args:
        action: ``show`` (default) to display the effective policy.
        changes: Partial policy to merge (``action='show'`` ignores it). Fields
            include ``enabled``, ``block_above``, ``approval_above``,
            ``warn_above``, ``redact_secrets``, ``fail_closed``,
            ``ignore_paths``, ``ignore_rules``, ``allow_secret_files``.

    Returns:
        ToolResponse: The effective policy as Markdown.

    Example:
        >>> security_policy()  # doctest: +SKIP
    """
    settings = _settings_of(kwargs)
    if not settings:
        raise Exception("Invalid project settings")

    stored: Dict[str, Any] = {}
    configured = getattr(settings, "settings", None)
    if isinstance(configured, dict) and isinstance(configured.get(ciso_policy.POLICY_SETTINGS_KEY), dict):
        stored = dict(configured[ciso_policy.POLICY_SETTINGS_KEY])

    if changes and action == "show":
        merged = dict(stored)
        merged.update(changes or {})
        validated = ciso_policy.policy_from_dict(merged)
        try:
            configured = getattr(settings, "settings", None)
            if isinstance(configured, dict):
                configured[ciso_policy.POLICY_SETTINGS_KEY] = validated.to_dict()
                save = getattr(settings, "save", None)
                if callable(save):
                    save()
            else:
                return ToolResponse(
                    user_response="⚠️ This project settings object does not expose a writable `settings` dict.",
                    llm_response="security_policy: unsupported settings object",
                )
        except Exception as ex:
            return ToolResponse(
                user_response=f"⚠️ Could not persist the policy: {ex}",
                llm_response=f"security_policy: persist failed: {ex}",
            )

    policy = resolve_policy(settings)
    markdown = _policy_markdown(policy, stored)
    return ToolResponse(
        user_response=markdown,
        llm_response=f"CISO policy: enabled={policy.enabled} "
                     f"block_above={policy.block_above.value} "
                     f"approval_above={policy.approval_above.value} "
                     f"fail_closed={policy.fail_closed}",
        logs=["CISO policy reported"],
    )


def _policy_markdown(policy: CisoPolicy, stored: Dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    """Render the effective policy as Markdown."""
    def _values(items) -> str:
        return ", ".join(f"`{item.value}`" for item in items) or "-"

    return "\n".join([
        "# CISO policy",
        "",
        f"- Enabled: **{policy.enabled}**",
        f"- Block severities: {_values(policy.block_severities)}",
        f"- Block categories: {_values(policy.block_categories)}",
        f"- Block above: `{policy.block_above.value}`",
        f"- Approval above: `{policy.approval_above.value}`",
        f"- Warn above: `{policy.warn_above.value}`",
        f"- Strict domains: {_values(policy.strict_domains)}",
        f"- Redact secrets: **{policy.redact_secrets}**",
        f"- Fail closed: **{policy.fail_closed}**",
        f"- Entropy threshold: `{policy.entropy_threshold}`",
        f"- Min secret length: `{policy.min_secret_length}`",
        "",
        "## Ignored paths",
        "```",
        "\n".join(policy.ignore_paths) or "-",
        "```",
        "## Silenced rules",
        "```",
        "\n".join(policy.ignore_rules) or "-",
        "```",
        "",
        f"_Stored overrides: {stored or 'none (defaults)'}_",
        "",
        "> Set `CODX_JUNIOR_CISO_DISABLED=1` in the environment for an emergency stop.",
    ])

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tool allowlist sentinels
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A profile whose ``tools`` allowlist contains this marker is granted EVERY
# chat-scoped tool registered in the runtime (the "codx-junior" harness profile
# uses it). The marker is expanded where the request tools are decided
# (:class:`codx.junior.ai.smol.smol_agent.SmolAgent`), so it never reaches the
# provider. Validators accept it as a tool name so a profile saved with it
# keeps working.
ALL_TOOLS_MARKER = "*"

# Tools that are NEVER granted by an allowlist, even with the marker: they are
# injected per run by the agent, which is the only component that knows whether
# the user may teach a profile (write access) or must only read knowledge.
PROFILE_MANAGED_TOOL_NAMES = frozenset({
    "profile_learning",
    "profile_knowledge",
    "profile_knowledge_search",
})


def all_tool_names() -> frozenset:
    """Return the names of every tool registered in the runtime."""
    return frozenset(tool["tool_json"]["function"]["name"] for tool in TOOLS)


def expand_tool_allowlist(selected) -> frozenset:
    """
    Expand a tool-name allowlist (e.g. ``Profile.tools``) into a name set.

    * ``ALL_TOOLS_MARKER`` ("*") grants every registered tool.
    * ``PROFILE_MANAGED_TOOL_NAMES`` are never granted by an allowlist: they
      are injected per run by the agent, which is the only component that
      knows whether the user may teach a profile (write access) or must only
      read knowledge.

    Args:
        selected: Iterable of tool names (may contain the marker).

    Returns:
        Frozen set of concrete tool names.
    """
    names = {str(name) for name in (selected or []) if name}
    if ALL_TOOLS_MARKER in names:
        names.discard(ALL_TOOLS_MARKER)
        names.update(all_tool_names() - PROFILE_MANAGED_TOOL_NAMES)
    return frozenset(names)

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tool allowlist sentinels
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A profile whose ``tools`` allowlist contains this marker is granted EVERY
# chat-scoped tool registered in the runtime (the "codx-junior" harness profile
# uses it). The marker is expanded where the request tools are decided
# (:class:`codx.junior.ai.smol.smol_agent.SmolAgent`), so it never reaches the
# provider. Validators accept it as a tool name so a profile saved with it
# keeps working.
ALL_TOOLS_MARKER = "*"

# Tools that are NEVER granted by an allowlist, even with the marker: they are
# injected per run by the agent, which is the only component that knows whether
# the user may teach a profile (write access) or must only read knowledge.
PROFILE_MANAGED_TOOL_NAMES = frozenset({
    "profile_learning",
    "profile_knowledge",
    "profile_knowledge_search",
})


def all_tool_names() -> frozenset:
    """Return the names of every tool registered in the runtime."""
    return frozenset(tool["tool_json"]["function"]["name"] for tool in TOOLS)


def expand_tool_allowlist(selected) -> frozenset:
    """
    Expand a tool-name allowlist (e.g. ``Profile.tools``) into a name set.

    * ``ALL_TOOLS_MARKER`` ("*") grants every registered tool.
    * ``PROFILE_MANAGED_TOOL_NAMES`` are never granted by an allowlist: they
      are injected per run by the agent, which is the only component that
      knows whether the user may teach a profile (write access) or must only
      read knowledge.

    Args:
        selected: Iterable of tool names (may contain the marker).

    Returns:
        Frozen set of concrete tool names.
    """
    names = {str(name) for name in (selected or []) if name}
    if ALL_TOOLS_MARKER in names:
        names.discard(ALL_TOOLS_MARKER)
        names.update(all_tool_names() - PROFILE_MANAGED_TOOL_NAMES)
    return frozenset(names)

"""
SmolAgent: a small, async-only OpenAI chat agent.

Compared to the removed :class:`codx.junior.ai.openai_ai.OpenAI_AI`, this
implementation:
    * exposes a single async ``chat()`` method (no sync variant),
    * uses an **iterative** tool loop instead of recursion,
    * delegates loop protection to :class:`LoopGuard`,
    * delegates logging, event emission and cancellation to
      :class:`engine.agent_runtime.AgentRunContext`,
    * keeps streaming, callbacks, cancellation and analytics.
    * caches tool results per conversation to avoid re-execution.
    * returns a typed :class:`AgentRunResult` (no untyped ``additional_kwargs``).
    * decides which profile tools to inject into the request (see
      :meth:`SmolAgent._profile_tools_for_run`): the profile definition itself
      never carries them.

Tool events (``TOOL_START`` / ``TOOL_END`` / ``TOOL_ERROR`` / ``TOOL_LOGS``) carry the
``tool_call_id``, the parsed JSON request args and a truncated result preview
so listeners (e.g. the ChatEventBridge) can surface tool executions as chat
messages in real time. ``TOOL_END`` additionally carries the dual-response tool's
user-facing ``output`` (see Message Structure below). Tool logs are emitted for
forensic audit trail.

Loop-Limit Handling
When :class:`LoopGuard` stops the run (max rounds, max tool calls or stuck
loop), the run is **not** aborted. Instead the tool-usage value is summarised
by the project's knowledge/RAG model and appended to the assistant answer, so
the findings survive in the persisted message and the next iteration can
continue without re-running the same tools. The summary request is
best-effort, does not count towards the loop limits, and its token usage is
recorded separately with the ``tool-analysis`` tag.

Tool-Limit Continuation (harness tasks)
The tool limits are a **guardrail**, not a stop condition for harness work. On
a harness turn (orchestration worker, run supervisor, delegated subagent or the
``codx-junior`` harness profile) that reaches a limit, the agent does NOT end
the turn: it injects a "path rethink" notice carrying every fact already
collected (deterministic ledger, no extra AI call) plus the instruction to use
fewer tools, change approach, or ask the user for the exact decision it needs,
and it renews the guard with a smaller budget (``TOOL_LIMIT_CONTINUATIONS``).
The turn only stops when the continuations are exhausted, and that stop is
reported as "needs a human decision" instead of a silent failure. Plain chats
keep the previous behaviour (stop + tool-usage summary).

Cost-Limit Handling
Every round (iteration) computes its cost in cxjcoins from the provider usage
and the model price settings, accumulates it into the chat total and reports it
on the returned :class:`AgentRunResult` (``result.cost``). Tools that report
their own cost through :attr:`ToolResponse.cost` are summed into both the
per-run total and the chat total. The chat total is seeded from ``Chat.cost``
(the accumulated, deletion-safe value maintained by ChatManager) so the budget
applies to the whole chat and is not reset when messages are deleted. When the
chat reaches its estimated cost (``Chat.estimation_cost``), the run stops
gracefully — before executing further tools — to keep the chat within budget.

Message Structure
A single final assistant message is always produced. Its ``content`` holds only
the model's own text: reasoning emitted between tool rounds plus the final
answer. Tool output is NO LONGER merged into the message content. For
dual-response tools, ``ToolResponse.user_response`` is emitted on the ``TOOL_END``
event and attached to the response message as a collapsible property
(``ToolEvent.output``), so the client decides how to render it (collapsed or
hidden) and the chat stays clean.

Profile tools
Profiles learn per project, so the tools that read/write what a profile has
learned are decided **per run** by this agent:

    * ``profile_knowledge_search`` — read-only, injected whenever profiles take
      part in the turn.
    * ``profile_learning`` — writes rules/knowledge files, injected only when
      the user is a project admin, a project knowledge admin
      (``knowledge_admin``) or a codx-junior admin.

The profiles participating in the turn are declared by the chat engine in an
internal ``profiles`` request header, which is consumed here and never
forwarded to the provider.

Vision API Support
Binary files (PDFs, images) are passed as vision content when models support it.
The content is merged into the final user message to enable vision-capable models
to process images and documents alongside text.

Error Visibility
Every AI provider interaction (the completion request, the streaming of its
response and the tool-usage summary request) is guarded so failures are logged
VERBATIM: phase, model, provider, endpoint, whether an API key is configured,
message/tool counts, request/chat/run identifiers, HTTP status, provider
``code``/``param``/``request_id``, provider request-id header, response body
(truncated) and the chained root cause (``httpx.ConnectError``, DNS, TLS,
timeout, proxy, ...) — always followed by a full traceback. A short Markdown
notice with the same details is also streamed to the client, because previously
a failed connection surfaced as nothing more than the provider's generic

def _iso_utc(epoch_seconds: float) -> str:
    """
    Format an epoch timestamp as an ISO-8601 UTC string.

    Used by the timing instrumentation (tool invocations and provider calls),
    where a wall-clock timestamp is needed next to the monotonic duration: the
    clock says *when* it happened (so lines from different components can be
    merged into one time frame) while the duration stays immune to clock jumps.

    Args:
        epoch_seconds: Value from ``time.time()``.

    Returns:
        An ISO-8601 string with millisecond precision and a ``Z`` suffix.
    """
    return datetime.utcfromtimestamp(epoch_seconds).strftime(
        "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%f"
    )[:-3] + "Z"


def _env_float(name: str, default: float) -> float:
    """Read a positive float from the environment (fallback on unset/invalid)."""
    raw = os.environ.get(name)
    if raw is None or not str(raw).strip():
        return default
    try:
        value = float(raw)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        logger.warning("SmolAgent: invalid %s=%r, using %.1f", name, raw, default)
        return default
    return value if value > 0 else default


def _env_int(name: str, default: int) -> int:
    """Read a non-negative int from the environment (fallback on unset/invalid)."""
    raw = os.environ.get(name)
    if raw is None or not str(raw).strip():
        return default
    try:

    except (TypeError, ValueError):

    or missing content causes it to re-issue the exact same tool call,

    - Empty lists/dicts
    - Zero (which is falsy but valid)
    - False boolean (which is falsy but valid)

        1. ``None``             → sentinel ``_TOOL_NO_OUTPUT``
        2. ``str``              → returned as-is (empty str → sentinel)
        3. ``dict``/``list``    → JSON-serialised for readability
        4. ``0`` or ``False``   → serialised as string (not sentinel!)
        5. Anything else        → ``str()`` fallback

            func_name,

    # Handle strings (including empty)

        if not result.strip():
            logger.debug(
                "SmolAgent: tool '%s' returned empty string – using sentinel",
                func_name,

            return json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False)
        try:
            return json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False)
        except (TypeError, ValueError):

    # These SHOULD be serialised, not replaced with sentinel

        return str(result)

    # Fallback: serialize any other type
    try:
        return json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        serialized = str(result)
        # Guard against empty string from str() fallback
        if not serialized.strip():
            logger.warning(
                "SmolAgent: tool '%s' returned %r which str() converted to empty string",
                func_name,
                result,
            )
            return _TOOL_NO_OUTPUT
        return serialized


def _format_ai_error(ex: BaseException) -> str:
    """
    Build a verbose, single-line description of an AI provider error.

    Connection failures against the LLM provider previously reached the logs
    only as ``str(ex)`` (e.g. ``"Connection error."``), which made them
    impossible to diagnose. This helper extracts every diagnostic the
    the OpenAI/httpx clients expose — HTTP status, error code/param, provider
    request id, response body — plus the chained root cause
    (``httpx.ConnectError``, ``socket.gaierror``, ``ReadTimeout``, TLS/proxy
    failures, ...) so the origin of the failure is visible from the log line
    alone.

    Args:
        ex: The exception raised while talking to the AI provider.

    Returns:
        A pipe-separated description of the error, safe for logging.
    """
    parts: List[str] = [f"type={type(ex).__name__}", f"message={ex}"]

    # Provider errors (openai.APIStatusError / APIConnectionError) may carry
    # an HTTP response with status code, headers and body.
    response = getattr(ex, "response", None)
    if response is not None:
        parts.append(f"http_status={getattr(response, 'status_code', '?')}")
        headers = getattr(response, "headers", None) or {}
        provider_request_id = None
        try:
            provider_request_id = (
                headers.get("x-request-id")
                or headers.get("request-id")
                or headers.get("x-litellm-call-id")
            )
        except (AttributeError, TypeError):
            # Defensive: unusual header container — request id is optional.
            provider_request_id = None
        if provider_request_id:
            parts.append(f"provider_request_id={provider_request_id}")
        body = ""
        try:
            body = response.text or ""
        except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - defensive: unreadable body
            body = ""
        if body:
            parts.append(f"body={body[:AI_ERROR_BODY_MAX_CHARS]}")

    # Attributes exposed directly by the provider client errors.
    for attr in ("code", "param", "status_code", "request_id", "body"):
        value = getattr(ex, attr, None)
        if value is not None:
            parts.append(f"{attr}={value}")

    # The real root cause (DNS, connection refused, timeout, TLS, proxy, ...)
    # is usually chained on the provider error.
    cause = ex.__cause__ or ex.__context__
    if cause is not None:
        parts.append(f"cause={type(cause).__name__}: {cause}")

    return " | ".join(str(part) for part in parts)


class SmolAgent:
    """
    Async-only streaming chat agent with multi-step tool support.

    All logging, event fan-out, cancellation checkpoints and per-run
    analytics are delegated to :class:`AgentRunContext` (the unified
    agent runtime). Callers may pass their own context through
    ``config["run_context"]`` (e.g. to share a Socket.IO listener or a
    cancellation token) or plain listeners via ``config["event_listeners"]``.

    Conversation flow
    ```mermaid
        flowchart TD
            A[chat] --> B[Resolve AgentRunContext]
            B --> C[run_context.run - RUN_START]
            C --> D[Build OpenAI messages]
            D --> E[Initialize ToolCache]
            E --> F[Stream completion via guard_stream]
            F -->|chunk| F1[Accumulate chunk]
            F1 -->|flush| F2[Callback with FULL accumulated content]
            F --> G{finish_reason?}
            G -->|tool_calls| H[Check ToolCache]
            H -->|HIT| H1[Skip _execute_tool - use cached]
            H -->|HIT| H2[Emit TOOL_END with cached=true]
            H -->|HIT - ToolResponse| H3[No output re-emitted - first run delivered it]
            H -->|MISS| I[LoopGuard.check - depth & breadth & stuck]
            I -->|ok| J[Execute tool - TOOL_START/END/ERROR/LOGS + output]
            H1 --> K{Dual-response tool?}
            J --> K
            K -->|yes| K1[user_response - collapsible TOOL_END output property]
            K -->|yes| K2[Send llm_response as tool result to model only]
            K -->|no| K3[Send normalised result as tool result to model only]
            K1 --> L[Append to openai_messages]
            K2 --> L
            K3 --> L
            L --> F
            I -->|limit exceeded| M[Summarise tool usage and finish gracefully]
            G -->|stop / length| N[Append final LLM text to final_answer_content]
            N --> O[Append final AIMessage + return typed AgentRunResult]
            M --> O
            O --> P[Record usage + cache stats - RUN_END]
            F -->|cancelled| Q[RUN_CANCELLED - raise CancelledError]
            F -->|provider error| R[Verbose AI error log + client notice - raise]
    ```
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        settings: CODXJuniorSettings,
        llm_model: Optional[str] = None,
        user: Optional[CodxUser] = None,
        system: Optional[str] = None,
        session: Optional[Any] = None,
        harness: bool = True,
    ) -> None:
        """
        Args:
            settings:  Project settings providing LLM configuration.
            llm_model: Optional model override.
            user:      Optional user (used for API key and analytics).
            system:    Optional extra system prompt content (appended after
                      chat_global_instructions).
            session:   Optional session context (injected for tools that need
                      access to current chat or session state).
            harness:   When False the run is a PLAIN completion: no agent
                      system prompt and no tool schemas. Use it for
                      single-shot prompts (docs assistant, enrichment) where
                      tool calling would only produce unusable output.
        """
        self.harness: bool = harness
        # Copy the registry: MCP tools are project-scoped and are appended to
        # this instance. Mutating the module-level TOOLS would leak one
        # project's CRM tools into every other project in the process.
        self.tools: List[Dict[str, Any]] = list(TOOLS)

        self.settings = settings
        self.llm_settings = settings.get_llm_settings(llm_model=llm_model)
        self.model: str = self.llm_settings.model
        self.user = user
        self.api_key: str = (
            user.api_key if user and user.api_key else self.llm_settings.api_key
        )
        self.base_url: str = self.llm_settings.api_url
        # Store extra system instructions; global instructions will be loaded
        # dynamically on each chat to ensure freshness
        self.extra_system: str = (system or "").strip()
        # Store session context for tools that need access to it
        self.session: Optional[Any] = session
        # Maximum seconds a single tool may run before it is aborted. A hung
        # tool used to block the whole chat turn (and the event loop) forever.
        # Priority: tool settings > model/provider > env > default.
        self.tool_timeout_seconds: float = self._resolve_tool_timeout_seconds()
        # How many independent tool calls of ONE round may run concurrently.
        # Most tools are I/O bound (file reads, HTTP, git/docker CLI), so a
